Drop Site Daily: October 2, 2026 | | | Oct 2 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Mourners standing closely around rows of Palestinian flag-draped shrouds during a mass funeral amid rubble in Gaza City, Gaza Strip, on October 1, 2026. Photo by Faiz Qreqa / Middle East Images / AFP via Getty Images. Friday, October 2, 2026 -** Iran : U.S. sending third carrier, up to 10,000 more troops to Middle East. U.S. deploys Patriot batteries to Saudi Arabia, Qatar. Treasury issues new round of sanctions on Iran's auto and rail sectors. Iran strikes fifth tanker in Hormuz within three days. Gulf oil exports double since early August. UK-Iranian national arrested over RAF Fairford incident. Yemen : Saudi-led coalition accuses Ansarallah of attack on power station serving holy city of Medina. President Donald Trump says Saudi Arabia "wouldn't be here" without him as defense chiefs hold call. Palestine: Israeli fire wounds three Palestinians in Khan Younis, including child. Israeli forces and settlers continue to attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank. Over 2,000 Israeli attacks on Palestinians in West Bank in September. Gaza families bury 105 Palestinians nearly three years after Israeli massacre. Hamas denies Israeli report on rebuilding military capabilities. Jared Kushner firm holds $1 billion stake in Israeli company invested in Gaza war suppliers. Lebanon: Israeli forces carry out strikes, demolitions and shelling across south Lebanon amid "ceasefire." U.S.: Supreme Court to hear challenge to Trump's mandatory immigration detention policy. South Korea denies finalizing funding for Trump's Alaska pipeline. Trump administration diverts $52M from Europe, Iraq to Latin America. Microsoft-linked NJ data center ran unpermitted generators for nearly a year, emitting hundreds of tons of pollution. Trump meme coin firm offers "most exclusive dinner" to top holders, raising fresh ethics concerns. Housing Finance agency guts its own inspector general. International: Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia. Ethiopian government-allied force claims to have wiped out TPLF forces in Tigray. U.S. waives human rights conditions for $320 million in aid to Egypt after the country's "helpful role" in Iran war. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his rival Flavio Bolsonaro skip final debate ahead of Sunday vote. Supreme Court bomb scare proves false alarm. Ousted Sudanese President Omar Al-Bashir, 82, wanted for genocide, needs treatment abroad. Russian President Vladimir Putin rules out ceasefire on long-range strikes, reiterates nuclear threat over Kaliningrad. India's "cockroach" party renews protests, demands election commissioner's resignation over voter roll dispute. Hundreds of schools remain closed in France as student protests grow. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. sending third carrier, up to 10,000 more troops to Middle East: The Pentagon is a third aircraft carrier strike group, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, to the Middle East, officials told the Wall Street Journal. The fleet reportedly left San Diego Sunday, alongside the USS Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. The latter will carry Marines from the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, adding 9,000 to 10,000 troops to a region that already has more than 50,000 U.S. personnel. These additional U.S. forces are expected to arrive in the region by the end of November. President Donald Trump reportedly told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran that same month. U.S. deploys Patriot batteries to Saudi Arabia, Qatar: The U.S. military two additional Patriot missile-defense batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar to protect key oil and gas facilities against potential Iranian retaliation if Trump resumes major strikes on Iran, Axios reported. The deployments come as Trump said Thursday he was considering renewed attacks in the coming weeks. "Now I have to make a decision: either Iran signs the deal, or it won't exist any longer," Trump said. Treasury issues new round of sanctions on Iran 's auto and rail sectors: The Treasury Department sanctions on Iran's rail and auto sectors and their foreign suppliers as part of Operation Economic Outcast. The sanctions affect Iran's two premier automotive companies, Iran Khodro and SAIPA, which together account for over 90% of the country's domestic market, as well as Iran's state-owned Islamic Republic of Iran Railway Company and two major passenger and freight rail firms. The new round of sanctions also targets foreign firms that supply Iran's auto companies, with affected firms in Indonesia, the UAE, and Turkey. Iran strikes fifth tanker in Hormuz within three days: Iran to have struck a fifth tanker in less than three days, according to recent incident reports from United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations. Between the evening of September 28 and October 1, five vessels were reported "struck by projectiles" while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the British maritime security body said. IRGC adviser Ali Balil claimed on Thursday that Iran achieved a longstanding goal of using a long-range ballistic missile to strike a moving target. Belali said the capability had been demonstrated "in the past few days," without identifying the target or providing further details. Gulf oil exports double since early August: Oil exports from the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman a seven-day average of around 20 million barrels per day, roughly double the early August amount, with Strait of Hormuz transits driving the rebound, according to Kpler data. The seven-day average of regional exports climbed from about 10 to 12 million barrels per day in early August to a peak of roughly 22 million in late September. Daily volumes briefly topped 27 million around September 19. Trump told reporters on Thursday the U.S. may ask European countries to release diesel reserves as U.S. diesel hit $6.53 per gallon. UK-Iranian national arrested over RAF Fairford incident: UK counter-terrorism police a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in connection with Sunday's incident near RAF Fairford, a U.S. Air Force-operated base. Five British men arrested near the base remain on police bail after gas, but no explosive devices, was found in vehicles. Police said they are investigating "all possible angles," including potential foreign-state involvement. Iran has strongly denied involvement. RAF Fairford has recently been used by U.S. bombers after Britain approved its use for strikes on Iran. Yemen Saudi-led coalition accuses Ansarallah of attack on power station serving holy city of Medina: The Saudi-led coalition Yemen's Ansarallah of carrying out a drone attack on the Taiba electricity distribution station in Islam's holy city of Medina, on September 29, saying an investigation and drone debris indicated the group was responsible. The attack knocked one transformer out of service but did not disrupt the electricity grid. The coalition previously accused Ansarallah of attempting to target Mecca, another Islamic holy site, allegations the group has denied. This comes amid continued fighting in Yemen. Saudi-backed government forces they carried out 20 air strikes over three hours targeting Ansarallah reinforcements across several fronts in Taiz, claiming the strikes destroyed military equipment and caused casualties. Government forces also said they downed Ansarallah drones over Aden and hit targets in the Ansarallah-held capital of Sana'a. Six people were killed and 35 wounded in overnight clashes between Ansarallah and government forces in residential areas of eastern Taiz, according to The Associated Press. Trump says Saudi Arabia "wouldn't be here" without him as defense chiefs hold call: Trump said Saudi Arabia "wouldn't be here right now" without him, claiming in a interview that both the kingdom and Israel would otherwise have been "wiped off the face of the planet." Trump said his relationship with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman remained "very good" and emphasized that the U.S. protects Saudi Arabia despite recent reporting that Trump denied MBS's request to enter its war against Ansarallah. Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman held a phone call with U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday to discuss the U.S.-Saudi defense coordination, according to the Saudi Press Agency. More than 100 U.S. military advisers are in Saudi Arabia providing intelligence, geospatial targeting support and battlefield technology for the kingdom's campaign against Ansarallah in Yemen. Palestine Israeli fire wounds three Palestinians in Khan Younis, including child: Two Palestinians, including an elderly woman, were by Israeli fire in Khan Younis early Friday, while a child was shot as Israeli forces fired toward tents east of Hamad City, according to WAFA. Civil Defense crews also recovered remains of a Palestinian killed in an Israeli drone strike in southern Gaza overnight. Israeli forces and settlers continue to attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank: Nablus: Three Palestinians were as Israeli settlers, backed by Israeli forces, attacked olive harvesters in Beita, Jamma'in, Urif, Asira al-Qibliya, Beit Furik, and Deir Sharaf on Friday, WAFA reported. Israeli forces also fired stun grenades and tear gas at Palestinian farmers and foreign solidarity activists. In a separate attack in Beita, settlers opened live fire toward farmers harvesting olives in the Jabal Al-Arma area, with no injuries reported. Salfit: Israeli forces and settlers farmers from harvesting olives west of Deir Istiya and forced others off their land in Farkha and Haris. Israeli forces also detained three farmers while they were harvesting olives on their land. Bethlehem: Israeli settlers a number of olive trees belonging to a Palestinian resident in the Abu Njeim area, southeast of Bethlehem. Jenin: Israeli forces a Palestinian after raiding and searching homes in Zababdeh, south of Jenin, and detained dozens of Palestinian workers in Barta'a, southwest of the city. Ramallah: Israeli settlers, accompanied by Israeli forces, homes south of Al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah, and stole a vehicle from the outskirts of the village. Over 2,000 Israeli attacks on Palestinians in West Bank in September: Israeli forces and settlers carried out over 2,000 attacks against Palestinians and their land and property in the month of September in the occupied West Bank, to the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. 1,404 of the attacks were carried out by Israeli military forces and 647 by Israeli settlers, while Ramallah and Al-Bireh recorded the most attacks. Settler attacks killed three Palestinians, bringing the total number of Palestinians killed by settlers in 2026 to 29. Attacks also damaged 14,600 trees, including 9,334 olive trees. Gaza families bury 105 Palestinians nearly three years after Israeli massacre: Hundreds gathered in Gaza City on Thursday for the mass funeral of 105 Palestinians killed on October 25, 2023, when Israeli forces dropped at least 20 bombs on the Al-Taj residential block and surrounding buildings in Yarmouk Square. Journalist Mahmoud Haniyeh, whose wife, journalist Doaa Sharaf, and their one-year-old son Obaida were killed in the Israeli attack, held up the child's belongings. "This is his baby bottle. This is his toy. And that is his shroud. I want to ask the world: What threat did this pose to Israel?" Haniyeh asked. Some 8,000 victims remain beneath destroyed buildings across Gaza, Civil Defense spokesperson Mahmoud Basal told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed. Basal called for the entry of equipment and logistical support needed to recover them. "If things remain as they are, we are talking about many years in which these families will remain beneath the rubble." Watch the dispatch from Mohamed Ahmed and . Hamas denies Israeli report on rebuilding military capabilities: Hamas denied an Israeli Channel 12 report claiming the group is accelerating efforts to rebuild its military apparatus, repair tunnels, and continue smuggling operations in Gaza. Spokesperson Hazem Qassem called the report "false" and said it was intended to justify continuing the war and cover up Israeli ceasefire violations. Qassem said Hamas remained committed to the ceasefire agreement and urged Trump's "Board of Peace" to adhere to the ceasefire plan and its associated roadmap, warning that providing Israel with "pretexts" would make the Board "a partner in the crimes committed in Gaza." Kushner firm holds $1 billion stake in Israeli company invested in Gaza war suppliers: Jared Kushner's investment firm is the in an Israeli financial company with at least $456 million invested in nine firms supplying Israel's military, CNN reported. Kushner's Affinity Partners holds a 7.4% stake in Phoenix Financial--worth over $1 billion. Phoenix's holdings include: $265 million in Elbit Systems, Israel's largest arms maker, $40 million in Reshef Technologies, which makes fuses for shells used in Gaza, and $68 million in Next Vision, which makes cameras for military drones. Phoenix also holds stakes in Caterpillar, whose D9 bulldozers are used by the Israeli military to ethnically cleanse communities in Gaza, other parts of occupied Palestine, and Lebanon. Kushner sits on the Board of Peace overseeing Gaza and Trump's "peace" plan. The White House called the conflict-of-interest concerns a "tired narrative." Lebanon Israeli forces carry out strikes, demolitions and shelling across south Lebanon amid "ceasefire": Tyre (Sour) district: Israeli forces two air strikes on Al-Mansouri and large explosions in Majdal Zoun on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli artillery also shelled Al-Mansouri and Wadi Zibqin. Bint Jbeil district: Israeli forces a large explosion in Aitaroun, shelled Beit Yahoun and Wadi al-Salouqi, and fired machine guns toward Hadatha and the outskirts of Bra'shit. U.S. News Supreme Court to hear challenge to Trump 's mandatory immigration detention policy: The Supreme Court Thursday to hear the Trump administration's appeal of a 2nd Circuit ruling against a July 2025 DHS policy subjecting millions of immigrants in deportation proceedings to mandatory detention without bond hearings. The case, involving Brazilian national Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha , who was denied a bond hearing after his September 2025 arrest in Massachusetts, will be argued in the court's new term beginning Monday. The policy has sparked more than 73,000 lawsuits--roughly a quarter of all federal civil cases filed this year--and judges have ruled over 4,400 times that detentions under the policy were unlawful, according to analysis from Reuters. South Korea denies finalizing funding for Trump 's Alaska pipeline: South Korea on President Trump's Oval Office announcement claiming Seoul had committed $54 billion to a long-stalled LNG pipeline in Alaska, with President Lee Jae Myung posting that the project "will proceed to working level under the preconditions that 1) its commercial viability is confirmed and 2) it complies with the legal procedures of the Republic of Korea," and the Korean government issuing a statement saying only that the two countries "have agreed to begin reviewing the project." Trump had made the announcement alongside Republican Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan , who is presently seeking reelection in a contested race. Trump claimed that Sullivan was "totally responsible for this pipeline" and explicitly tied the funding push to Sullivan's electoral prospects. Trump administration diverts $52M from Europe, Iraq to Latin America: The Trump administration a hold placed by Sen. Jeanne Shaheen(D-N.H.) and Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), notifying Congress late Wednesday that it would move forward with diverting $52 million in military assistance originally approved for Slovakia, North Macedonia, Tunisia, and Iraq to Panama, Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia instead. In a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio , Shaheen and Meeks said the move violated statutory requirements, noting that the Slovakia and North Macedonia funds came from a Ukraine supplemental bill specifically intended for countries affected by Russia's invasion. The State Department defended the reallocation as consistent with the National Security Strategy's focus on the Western Hemisphere, saying it would "combat narco-terrorism" and help "secure the Panama Canal." Microsoft-linked NJ data center ran unpermitted generators for nearly a year, emitting hundreds of tons of pollution: DataOne, a New Jersey data center with ties to Microsoft that was recently fined $1 million for running unpermitted generators, 62 gas-fired generators for more than 46,000 combined hours starting in July 2025 before state regulators intervened, according to reporting from The Guardian. An analysis by Rutgers professor Xiaomeng Jin estimated the generators emitted about 140 tons of NOx, a class of dangerous, smog-producing gases, enough to rank DataOne among New Jersey's top five NOx polluters in 2025. The company's CEO had told a January town hall the site would be "polluting less than a farm." Trump meme coin firm offers "most exclusive dinner" to top holders, raising fresh ethics concerns: GetTrumpMemes.com, the firm behind Trump's "$TRUMP" meme coin, a new competition Wednesday promising its 185 largest coin holders an invitation to a gala "evening with 3 Legends and President Donald J. Trump," with the top 29 purchasers getting a VIP reception and the top four receiving an 18-karat Trump-branded gold watch. Trump has earned $635 million from the meme coin since it was created last year, part of $1.4 billion in disclosed earnings from business ventures in 2025; purchasers of the coin have collectively lost an estimated $4.7 billion, according to the watchdog group Public Citizen. Housing Finance agency guts its own inspector general: Bill Pulte , the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, plans to cut staffing at agency's inspector general office by 70-80% in fiscal year 2027, which staff told Congress would force the office to "discontinue essentially all criminal investigations" and effectively "wind down its operations." The move follows the November removal of the agency's acting inspector general Joe Allen after Democrats had asked him to investigate Pulte's "troubling and unprecedented politicization" of the agency's investigative powers against Trump's perceived political enemies, including Sen. Adam Schiff and New York Attorney General Letitia James. Treasury releases rules for nation 's first federal school voucher program: The Treasury Department rules Thursday governing the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, the first federally funded school voucher program, which offers taxpayers up to $1,700 in reimbursement for every dollar donated to "scholarship-granting organizations," which will then pass along the money to families. It is projected to cost $26 billion in lost federal revenue over 10 years. States have until January 1 to opt in, with 30 mostly Republican-led states already announcing their intention to join in the program. American Federation of Teachers President Randi Weingarten urged governors to reject the program, calling it "a poison pill for the 90% of American children who attend public schools." Senators respond to Collins corruption allegations: A ProPublica investigation published on September 22 found that the Department of Justice's public corruption unit, just before it was gutted by President Donald Trump, was circling Maine Republican Senator Susan Collins after her campaign solicited illegal contributions from a Hawaii-based defense contractor. The company, Navatek, sent $150,000 to Collins's super PAC through a shell company; $32 million in federal contracts were funneled to the company shortly after. Drop Site's Julian Andreone asked senators on Capitol Hill about this reporting. His interviews are available. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia: Eritrea Thursday it is breaking diplomatic relations with Ethiopia after Addis Ababa expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats, including the charge d'affaires, declaring them personae non gratae because they had participated in "activities that pose a direct threat to Ethiopia's national security." Eritrea's foreign ministry called Ethiopia's accusations "astounding," countering that "it is Ethiopia which has been pursuing an agenda of incessant hostility" and accusing Addis Ababa of waging war to gain Red Sea access and training Eritrean opposition groups. Ethiopia separately expelled an Egyptian diplomat; Egypt reciprocated by expelling an Ethiopian embassy official in Cairo. Addis Ababa has accused Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt of backing the opposition alliance, led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front, now fighting its federal forces. Ethiopian government-allied force claims to have wiped out TPLF forces in Tigray: A commander in the Tigray Peace Forces, which is allied with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government, late Thursday that TPLF forces had been "wiped out" from the province as government forces closed in on the regional capital, according to Reuters. The TPLF acknowledged federal forces had occupied parts of the region but said his forces would "counter-attack in due course." U.S. waives human rights conditions for $320 million in aid to Egypt after the country 's "helpful role" in Iran war: The State Department human rights certification requirements for $320 million in annual military financing to Egypt, citing Cairo's "helpful role" in the U.S.'s war on Iran, according to a September 21 letter to Congress signed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and reported on by Reuters. The memo did not elaborate on the details of that "help." Egypt is the second largest recipient of U.S. military aid in the world, receiving roughly $1.3 billion annually since the 1980s following its 1979 peace treaty with Israel. While small portions of aid to Egypt have been withheld in the past, granting a national security waiver to override human rights concerns is now routine. In September 2024, the Biden administration issued a waiver to grant the full $1.3 billion allocation, citing Egypt's assistance to the U.S. around Israel's war on Gaza. Brazil 's Lula, Bolsonaro skip final debate ahead of Sunday vote; Supreme Court bomb scare proves false alarm: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his rival Flavio Bolsonaro both a planned TV Globo debate Thursday, the last before Sunday's first-round presidential election, with Lula instead appearing on a popular podcast and Bolsonaro blaming "censorship imposed by the electoral court" after a ruling barred the broadcaster from leaving Lula's seat empty onstage. TV Globo said the cancellation stemmed from "legal uncertainty" created by conflicting rulings from Brazil's electoral and supreme courts. Brazilian police also arrested a suspect who tried to jump the Supreme Court's fences and threw a backpack onto a bus stop, believing that he may have been carrying an explosive. The backpack contained only personal belongings, authorities said, and the man remains in custody. Congo displacement camp abandoned after military raid, heightening fears of Ebola outbreak: Thousands of residents DRC's Kigonze camp in the Ituri province, home to about 19,000 displaced people, Congolese and UN officials reported on Thursday, after soldiers searching for weapons entered the site last week and clashes broke out. The camp now lies abandoned, officials said, and a facility where Ebola cases were isolated and treated was burned down. Health officials said roughly 1,000 Ebola contacts had been living in the camp, and that roughly a fifth of these have been traced since the exodus began. Congo's Ebola outbreak has recorded over 4,000 deaths, according to the latest figures, making up nearly half of the 8,300 confirmed cases, in the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Ousted Sudanese President Bashir, 82, wanted for genocide, needs treatment abroad : Omar al-Bashir, who ruled Sudan for three decades before being toppled in 2019, has been from military custody in Merowe to a military-run hospital in Khartoum for medical tests, his lawyer Mohamed Alhassan Alameen told Reuters on Thursday, saying that symptoms he has exhibited require diagnosis and treatment outside Sudan. His family echoed the calls for him to be transported out of the country, and noted that they had not yet received permission to do so; it remains unclear what condition he is suffering from. Bashir, who was convicted on charges of corruption and illicit financing after his ouster in 2019, is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of genocide; in addition to these, he faces several open cases in Sudan. Putin rules out ceasefire on long-range strikes, reiterates nuclear threat over Kaliningrad : Russian President Vladimir Putin a ceasefire on long-range strikes with Ukraine at Moscow's Valdai forum Thursday, calling the idea "simply ridiculous" days after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv was ready to halt strikes on Russian refineries if Moscow reciprocated on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Putin repeated his warning that Russia would deploy "all the weapons at our country's disposal" if NATO attempted to cut off the Kaliningrad exclave, following a diplomatic note Moscow sent NATO this week threatening nuclear action in such a scenario and cautioned against "the logic of escalating," in which "increasingly harsh retaliatory measures [lead] to a fatal point of no return." NATO has not made overt threats to sever Russian access to Kaliningrad though recent military exercises near the territory and naval patrols in the Baltic Sea have raised concerns in Moscow. In Putin's speech, he reiterated his preference for ending the war through talks, and for a "neutral Ukraine." He also suggested that, under a "favorable scenario," Russia might return the assets of Western companies which it seized at the beginning of the war. Greece pushes EU to allow asylum suspensions during migration emergencies : Greece the European Union to let member states temporarily suspend asylum applications during periods of mass migration. The country's Migration Minister, Thanos Plevris, argued at a meeting of interior ministers in Luxembourg that the bloc's migration pact, in effect since June, has "not gone far enough" and that emergencies warrant "enhanced border surveillance and suspension of asylum." Plevris was backed by Dutch Migration Minister Bart van den Brink, who argued that recent surges like the July incident in Spain's Ceuta exclave should be "treated as a border management issue rather than an asylum issue." Ministers also approved a new regulation allowing member states to establish migrant "return hubs" outside the EU, with recent reports suggesting that the "Group of Five" nations (Greece, the Netherlands, Germany, Austria and Denmark) were considering Rwanda to host such a site. India 's "cockroach" party renews protests, demands election commissioner's resignation over voter roll dispute: India's Gen Z-led Cockroach Janata Party, alongside a separate coalition of student and activist groups, is fresh protests Friday in Mumbai and New Delhi, demanding the resignation of Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations that his commission manipulated voter rolls to favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's right-wing Bharatiya Janata Party. The commission and government deny the allegations. Pressure intensified after India's Indian Express newspaper reported Kumar's two deputies had formally raised concerns at least 14 times over the past 10 months regarding revisions to voter lists and the commission's digital systems. The CJP, led by Abhijeet Dipke, gained prominence earlier this year after forcing the resignation of India's education minister, who was embroiled in a scandal involving leaked exam papers and was blamed for rising unemployment in the country. Hundreds of schools remain closed in France as student protests grow: Student protests across France over a host of grievances including teacher shortages and dilapidated school buildings, have continued to grow forcing the closure of some 400 schools on Friday. Police have cracked down on the protests, arresting nearly 3,000 people, 90% of them minors, to France24. Around 170 students and 65 staff members--including 40 school principals--have been injured. Over 100 high schools have suffered severe damage. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu called a crisis cabinet meeting on Thursday and told ministers to cancel travel plans to deal with the demonstrations. Hungary signals easing opposition to Ukraine 's EU membership: The Hungarian government said that it draft Ukrainian legislation Friday that would strengthen Hungarian-language education for Ukraine's roughly 100,000 ethnic Hungarians, as part of talks to lift its objections to possible Ukrainian integration into the European Union. Friend: In a moment, I'm going to share with you my vision for New Mexico — **_[but first, can I ask you to take 30 seconds to personally endorse my campaign for Governor?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202610_endorse_vision?source=jtk1462-su-nd&t=2&akid=12873%2E400544%2E_ZZozT)_**
| | [Add My Name](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202610_endorse_vision?source=jtk1462-su-nd&t=3&akid=12873%2E400544%2E_ZZozT)
---
This message is a bit on the longer side, but because you're invested in the future of New Mexico, I hope you'll take the time to read my plan. **As New Mexico’s next Governor, I will:**
**Build Education That Works for New Mexico by:**
* Ensuring students can read before third grade by identifying literacy challenges early and providing targeted support when children fall behind

* Strengthening early literacy screening, expanding bilingual and reading instruction, and investing in summer reading and after-school programs that reinforce learning beyond the school day

* Bolstering access to universal childcare, because learning begins long before a child enters a classroom

* Directing unspent dollars from the Public School Capital Outlay Fund to modernize and improve school facilities so kids can focus on learning

* Expanding outdoor and place-based learning through my Every Child Outdoor Initiative, giving schools the tools and resources to connect classroom instruction to real-world learning that improves engagement and outcomes

**Support New Mexico Families by:**
* Raising the minimum wage and eliminating predatory junk fees

* Passing Paid Family and Medical Leave so people don’t have to choose between caring for their family and making ends meet

* Increasing the child tax credit to put money back into your pockets

* Creating a statewide tenant bill of rights to make renting more affordable and more transparent

* Creating a Critical Sector Housing Fund for workers in critical sectors — like healthcare, behavioral health, social work, education, and more — to recruit more professionals to New Mexico to address endemic shortages that hold our people back

* Aggressively building more housing, eliminating unnecessary red tape, driving state investment into housing, and shortening the time it takes to build a home — and ensuring those homes are built with New Mexican labor

**Back Small Businesses by:**
* Establishing a permanent Office of Small Business to coordinate development programs, fill gaps left by federal cuts, and provide clear access to grants, capital, and state resources

* Cracking down on predatory lending by requiring full transparency in small-business loan disclosures

* Establishing a New Mexico Economic Growth Trust Fund to stabilize our economy in the face of federal uncertainty

**Fix Our Broken Healthcare System by:**
* Protecting and expanding access to healthcare in every part of New Mexico

* Banning medical debt from being included on credit reports

* Expanding New Mexico’s Health Care Affordability Fund to protect access for those who rely on the state marketplace

* Using budget surpluses to fill Medicaid gaps and hire more guides to help people enroll in and keep their benefits

* Ensuring sustainable funding for rural hospitals and clinics, expanding mobile health clinics, and significantly increasing access to outpatient behavioral and mental health care, including a full-scale effort to deliver mental health and homelessness assistance statewide

**Strengthen Public Safety by:**
* Ensuring that law enforcement has the tools, staffing, and technology they need to do their jobs effectively

* Investing in mental and behavioral healthcare and housing stability

* Expanding violence intervention and prevention programs in schools and communities, building accountability systems that emphasize fairness and trust, and investing in community policing models that supplement traditional police work

* Creating a statewide Department of Community Safety staffed with social workers and counselors so law enforcement can focus on violent crime while people get the help they need

* Requiring ICE agents to clearly identify themselves and prohibiting masks that shield misconduct from accountability

New Mexico deserves steady leadership that’s ready on day one, leadership rooted in firsthand knowledge and experience. But the only way we'll be able to make this vision a reality is with strong grassroots support from people like you.
**I'm aiming to get 10,000 endorsements for my campaign before my midnight deadline to show the grassroots strength behind my vision for New Mexico, and I want you to be one of them._[Will you please take a quick moment to sign on now?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202610_endorse_vision?source=jtk1462-su-nd&t=4&akid=12873%2E400544%2E_ZZozT)_**

clean_body: | | | Friend: In a moment, I'm going to share with you my vision for New Mexico — | | This message is a bit on the longer side, but because you're invested in the future of New Mexico, I hope you'll take the time to read my plan. As New Mexico’s next Governor, I will: Build Education That Works for New Mexico by: Ensuring students can read before third grade by identifying literacy challenges early and providing targeted support when children fall behind Strengthening early literacy screening, expanding bilingual and reading instruction, and investing in summer reading and after-school programs that reinforce learning beyond the school day Bolstering access to universal childcare, because learning begins long before a child enters a classroom Directing unspent dollars from the Public School Capital Outlay Fund to modernize and improve school facilities so kids can focus on learning Expanding outdoor and place-based learning through my Every Child Outdoor Initiative, giving schools the tools and resources to connect classroom instruction to real-world learning that improves engagement and outcomes Support New Mexico Families by: Raising the minimum wage and eliminating predatory junk fees Passing Paid Family and Medical Leave so people don’t have to choose between caring for their family and making ends meet Increasing the child tax credit to put money back into your pockets Creating a statewide tenant bill of rights to make renting more affordable and more transparent Creating a Critical Sector Housing Fund for workers in critical sectors — like healthcare, behavioral health, social work, education, and more — to recruit more professionals to New Mexico to address endemic shortages that hold our people back Aggressively building more housing, eliminating unnecessary red tape, driving state investment into housing, and shortening the time it takes to build a home — and ensuring those homes are built with New Mexican labor Back Small Businesses by: Establishing a permanent Office of Small Business to coordinate development programs, fill gaps left by federal cuts, and provide clear access to grants, capital, and state resources Cracking down on predatory lending by requiring full transparency in small-business loan disclosures Establishing a New Mexico Economic Growth Trust Fund to stabilize our economy in the face of federal uncertainty Fix Our Broken Healthcare System by: Protecting and expanding access to healthcare in every part of New Mexico Banning medical debt from being included on credit reports Expanding New Mexico’s Health Care Affordability Fund to protect access for those who rely on the state marketplace Using budget surpluses to fill Medicaid gaps and hire more guides to help people enroll in and keep their benefits Ensuring sustainable funding for rural hospitals and clinics, expanding mobile health clinics, and significantly increasing access to outpatient behavioral and mental health care, including a full-scale effort to deliver mental health and homelessness assistance statewide Strengthen Public Safety by: Ensuring that law enforcement has the tools, staffing, and technology they need to do their jobs effectively Investing in mental and behavioral healthcare and housing stability Expanding violence intervention and prevention programs in schools and communities, building accountability systems that emphasize fairness and trust, and investing in community policing models that supplement traditional police work Creating a statewide Department of Community Safety staffed with social workers and counselors so law enforcement can focus on violent crime while people get the help they need Requiring ICE agents to clearly identify themselves and prohibiting masks that shield misconduct from accountability New Mexico deserves steady leadership that’s ready on day one, leadership rooted in firsthand knowledge and experience. But the only way we'll be able to make this vision a reality is with strong grassroots support from people like you. I'm aiming to get 10,000 endorsements for my campaign before my midnight deadline to show the grassroots strength behind my vision for New Mexico, and I want you to be one of them. | | Thank you for your support, Deb | | | | | |

Friends,

**Governor Newsom just signed SB 1379.**
This bill was authored by DSA State Sen. Sabrina Cervantes. Now she and Sacramento have used state power to strip me of an office the voters of Riverside County elected me to serve.
I was elected Sheriff and public Coroner. That is how 48 of California’s 58 counties still operate. One person. One department. Local control.SB 1379 does not apply to those other 57 counties. It targets Riverside County. **It targets me**.
---
| | | | | [Support Bianco](https://us.list-manage.com/o9uFo98AVi3?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |
The Democrat-majority Board of Supervisors now has to appoint a separate official and set up an entirely new department — staff, building, bureaucracy — while the county is already staring at a nearly $70 million deficit. Taxpayers will pay for a political hit job.This is not reform. **This is political weaponization**.
The same Democrat supervisors already shorted my department by $125 million. That is not “oversight.” **This is defund the police**.
Look at the pattern.They defunded the Sheriff’s Office. They passed a law to stop sheriffs from examining ballots that are the subject of a criminal investigation. The California Supreme Court then piled on. Now they carve the Coroner’s Office away from the only county they decided to single out.
This is what one-party rule looks like when it cannot beat you at the ballot box: change the rules. Isolate one official.
**Stand with me. Contribute what you can. Help me fight this.**

Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County

clean_body: Must read | | | | | | | Friends, Governor Newsom just signed SB 1379. This bill was authored by DSA State Sen. Sabrina Cervantes. subject: Remove Pete Hegseth From Office for War Crimes

body:
United Nations investigators now say there are reasonable grounds to conclude that the Minab strike was a war crime.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2497%2E791427%2EwtYuNY)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/6528?t=2&akid=2497%2E791427%2EwtYuNY)
Friend — on the first day of Trump’s stupid, needless war with Iran, US missiles hit a school in Minab, Iran, killing over 150 people, including at least 123 children.
United Nations investigators now say there are reasonable grounds to conclude that this strike was a war crime. Seven months later, ‘Secretary of War’ Pete Hegseth has refused to take responsibility or hold anyone accountable.
[**Before I go on, if that’s all you need to hear, sign my petition calling for Pete Hegseth to be removed from office. Otherwise, please read on:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_hegseth_pet_oct26/?source=em261002-1-180&refcode2=2497.791427.wtYuNY&akid=2497%2E791427%2EwtYuNY)
**[SIGN ON NOW](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_hegseth_pet_oct26/?source=em261002-1-180&refcode2=2497.791427.wtYuNY&akid=2497%2E791427%2EwtYuNY)**
This new reporting from Bloomberg makes it clear: Trump and Hegseth knew they were responsible for the Minab attack, and have been shielding themselves from accountability.
Think about this: Trump has suggested that Iran bombed their own civilians, and as recently as July, he said: “I don’t think anybody’s going to ever be able to say what happened there.” But now we know that’s a lie — Pentagon officials knew **within hours** that the US was responsible for the strike.
So why has it taken over seven months for Pete Hegseth to deliver on his promise of an investigation into what happened? It turns out, they are dragging their feet:
“Previous news reports have indicated that by early March, a preliminary internal review determined the US was likely responsible for the Minab strike. A report on the full Pentagon investigation, which commenced in March, hasn’t been released — though the officials said it has been all-but-complete for several months.”
Perhaps because this investigation would place a major part of the blame on Hegseth’s decision to intentionally dismantle most of the Pentagon’s civilian harm mitigation units, who are responsible for making sure incidents like these never happen.
**In other words, our military committed a heinous war crime under Pete Hegseth’s command, and he’s working to cover it up.**
And this isn’t Pete Hegseth’s first time committing war crimes.
Over 200 people have been executed by US forces striking boats in the Caribbean under Hegseth’s command. No due process. No direct threat to the US. No confirmation that the people in the boats are combatants. In fact, many of these boats turned out to be carrying fishermen and laborers.
Hegseth even personally ordered that US commanders “kill everybody” on board these boats, including survivors — a clear war crime.
**If this administration won’t abide by international law, then it’s up to us to push for consequences for these criminals.**
[**Add your name today and help us show grassroots support for removing Pete Hegseth as Secretary of War. He’s an incompetent, unqualified, and dangerous man who has been responsible for killing hundreds, if not thousands, of civilians. Justice must come.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_hegseth_pet_oct26/?source=em261002-1-180&refcode2=2497.791427.wtYuNY&akid=2497%2E791427%2EwtYuNY)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_hegseth_pet_oct26/?source=em261002-1-180&refcode2=2497.791427.wtYuNY&akid=2497%2E791427%2EwtYuNY)**
The American people are sick and tired of warmongering leaders in Washington who have no problem wasting trillions of dollars on needless wars, death, and destruction.
That money would be better spent here at home, repairing and improving lives rather than destroying them. That idea is central to this movement, and why we must always fight for accountability in the face of endless wars.
In solidarity,
Ilhan Omar

| | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won.** _**They still are not stopping. **_ **The Constitution hasn't changed**. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. clean_body: I don’t want to make light of what’s at stake for each of us. | = I woke up this morning with immense gratitude for this movement and the people that power it. Before I say anything else, I just want to say: thank you. Because of your support, our team has been able to scale up our operations across the country to elect climate champions. As we approach the last month of the campaign season, the stakes for our planet – and for us – are becoming impossible to ignore. Corporate tech giants are building massive AI data centers in our communities. These water-guzzling facilities are highly unpopular. They require enormous amounts of energy and divert clean water to cool the servers powering the profits of tech billionaires. But grassroots leaders are stepping forward to protect their neighborhoods' air, water, and power grids: ✊ William Lawrence (Michigan): Running for Congress in a highly competitive purple district, Will has made unchecked data center expansion a key focus of his campaign. He’s pushing for national policy that puts real guardrails on the industry, giving us a rare opportunity to send a leader to Washington who can help shape how our country confronts this issue. 📢 Joanna Whaley (Michigan): Defeated an incumbent in the HD-2 primary to tackle community concerns over job loss and unchecked data center development. 🗳️ Myrna Muñoz (Oregon): Unseated an incumbent to fight for a state senate seat, demanding a three-year moratorium on new large-scale data centers in her district. Data centers might be a relatively new political issue, but dumping environmental harms onto our most vulnerable neighbors is a story as old as time. That’s why I’m truly amazed by the leaders we’ve endorsed this year – they represent a new generation of climate champions with real plans to hold these corporations accountable and protect the communities being forced to bear the costs. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Every movement I’ve been part of has ultimately been defined by people — ordinary people deciding that the status quo is unacceptable and doing something about it. Hi, I’m Ken Burns, a filmmaker who has, for nearly half a century, been telling America’s story. New Hampshire is my home. Which is why I’m proud to endorse Cinde Warmington for Governor.

Cinde Warmington will stand up for New Hampshire. And we need her now more than ever.

**[Will you join me and chip in $50 to help elect Cinde Warmington as our next Governor?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvfSUzEwI75hfq5cyeleu2wBzzH1ShcGjcxuLUdNJian6kgGn-JhjpI3ASy28DTYOO82TDGSbImflF9thdpNaiMZvHf85OGb6V97cJG8QoPcUWsyRkP7k_E0MBm3PYtEReDwVYrpjJDv7MJ507hf-cUHf2Bdl8-hhLydwz2X5IxE_1dI7Z3JGB9jKD9PFpe6GFht17Fe30KqJLKDnGtxWbRNrgbLZyPIGd4pcsqOfp7aoS5mEx6TfJgbJ4F4YOs9X9Fkg8csGGtj_n3cODj-xMf32rJe6PxYl9JLrlLDF7woMsV2CmKvcJsUOLYrYrBf90JYLh-XxOhq6uG-hdI8Mx3/4uj/74raYP1aTlGoL15UkNJnBg/h1/h001.ydh6ChW3kVLo74BnXSxRwRUFX4lfiprrUrqeMX9IZsE)**

With a president in Washington whose policies are crushing working families – higher costs for gas, groceries, housing, health care, and now, as colder weather approaches, for heating oil – the clear lack of leadership in Concord is devastating.

As a member of the Executive Council, Cinde stood up for our families, often the lone voice taking on those who would restrict our fundamental rights and opportunities.

New Hampshire deserves a leader in the corner office who puts Granite Staters first.

I’m proud to endorse Cinde. I hope you will join me in supporting her campaign and contributing today so New Hampshire has a Governor truly for New Hampshire – working for us all.

Those who have remained silent while our Republic has been attacked from within do not deserve our vote!

clean_body: | | | Hi, I’m Ken Burns, a filmmaker who has, for nearly half a century, been telling America’s story. New Hampshire is my home. Which is why I’m proud to endorse Cinde Warmington for Governor. Cinde Warmington will stand up for New Hampshire. And we need her now more than ever. With a president in Washington whose policies are crushing working families – higher costs for gas, groceries, housing, health care, and now, as colder weather approaches, for heating oil – the clear lack of leadership in Concord is devastating. As a member of the Executive Council, Cinde stood up for our families, often the lone voice taking on those who would restrict our fundamental rights and opportunities. New Hampshire deserves a leader in the corner office who puts Granite Staters first. I’m proud to endorse Cinde. I hope you will join me in supporting her campaign and contributing today so New Hampshire has a Governor truly for New Hampshire – working for us all. Those who have remained silent while our Republic has been attacked from within do not deserve our vote! Yesterday's attempted murder of Maine Wire journalist Joe Sokol was an act of targeted political violence. In the phone interview I recorded with the driver, he made clear that he has consumed both a ton of taxpayer-funded narcotics from Discovery House and a ton of Joe's content on Facebook. Joe has reported at length on drug addiction, crime, and failed harm-reduction policies in Bangor. The assailant did not like Joe's perspective on those issues and tried to silence him -- first through intimidation, then through violence. Anyone with eyes can see that the intent was to cause Joe deadly harm.

For the leftists who claim that Joe's presence at public parks, or his coverage of taxpayer-funded institutions from public property, is incitement or agitation -- that is the same argument that blames a woman for her rape because she wore a short skirt. Those who make such claims should not be taken seriously. Their only intention is to legitimize more violence against Maine Wire reporters. Vagrants and drug addicts who terrorize our public spaces, despoil our parks, and make our streets unsafe are not a protected class with a right to open drug use and anti-social behavior. Their conduct -- and municipal officials' growing willingness to tolerate it -- is inherently newsworthy.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..kfsQcP-bKonDSqvs_GZXRK3i8FCTWjT2PqS1pRstc3o?)
Others are trying to minimize the attempted murder of a journalist by calling the Maine Wire a conservative outlet. If exposing transnational organized crime, hundreds of millions of dollars in welfare fraud, systemic political corruption, and the inhumane abuse of disabled Americans at taxpayer-funded group homes is conservative, then what exactly is non-conservative journalism? What is liberal journalism? We'll proudly wear the label, because it means we report on what actually matters to Mainers rather than serving as stenographers for the people in power who have caused so much misery in this state.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=218527335&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE4NTI3MzM1LCJpYXQiOjE3OTA5NTk4MjIsImV4cCI6MTc5MzU1MTgyMiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.VYlmXvkoDXHiz8g8aMMAPMtbTNCVtUJTr4SGR0jQL8k)
The attempted murder of Joe Sokol is only the latest in a string of violence directed at Maine Wire journalists. Our reporters have been assaulted multiple times just this year, had their property vandalized, and been harassed at their homes. If the same targeted political violence were directed at another group because of race, religion, or politics, it would rightly cause a statewide and national uproar. Instead, Maine's elected officials, including Gov. Janet Mills and Attorney General Aaron Frey, remain silent. One would think Charlie Kirk's murder would have prompted some reflection from leftist leaders who foment this kind of hatred and violence. Sadly, the past year has shown otherwise.
Our work speaks for itself. The quality, integrity, and fearlessness of our investigative journalism is why, in less than four years, we have become the most influential news platform in Maine, if not New England. We will continue undaunted.

The following report examines findings from four key articles authored by independent researchers, journalists, and medical professionals regarding COVID-19 vaccine safety concerns--particularly around pregnancy risks, suppressed government communications, and legal liability shields. These sources, operating outside mainstream institutional channels, have raised critical questions that establishment media, government agencies, and professional medical organizations have largely failed to address or actively downplayed.

**I. False Claims About Miscarriage Risk: Jessica Rose**
Author: Jessica Rose, PhD (Data Scientist, Substack)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/68aac868-c927-493b-9024-7e9b0dac9665?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In her Substack analysis titled "False Claims About Miscarriage Risk" (jessicar.substack.com), Dr. Jessica Rose examines the intersection of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination and pregnancy outcomes through independent data analysis. Rose, who holds a doctorate in computational biology and has specialized in analyzing VAERS (Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System) data, challenges mainstream media narratives that have uniformly dismissed concerns about miscarriage risks.

Rose's research identifies significant signals in adverse event databases that she argues were inadequately investigated by regulatory agencies. Her work highlights how early theoretical concerns raised by immunologists--regarding the potential for mRNA vaccine components to trigger inflammatory responses that could threaten early pregnancy--were dismissed rather than rigorously studied. She documents instances where peer-reviewed studies showing elevated miscarriage signals were subjected to unusual retractions or buried beneath reassuring headlines that misrepresented the actual data.

What distinguishes Rose's contribution is her insistence on following the raw data rather than accepting institutional assurances. She has repeatedly noted that the established reproductive immunology raised legitimate theoretical concerns at the outset of the vaccine rollout--concerns that were brushed aside in the rush to vaccinate pregnant women without completing standard reproductive toxicology studies.

**II. "How A Pregnant Nurse Knew mRNA Vaccination Was Wrong"**
Publication: The Focal Points (Substack)
Key Figure: Adara Allen (Featured Subject)

Published in The Focal Points (thefocalpoints.com), this article tells the story of Adara Allen, a pregnant nurse who made the difficult decision to refuse mRNA COVID-19 vaccination and ultimately gave up her job rather than comply with mandates. Allen's account illustrates how frontline healthcare workers--those closest to patient care--were often the first to recognize warning signs that administrators and policymakers ignored.

Allen reportedly observed patterns in her clinical setting that raised immediate red flags: the absence of completed reproductive safety trials, the novel mechanism of mRNA technology distributed systemically rather than remaining localized at injection sites, and the unprecedented nature of pushing an experimental platform on pregnant women without long-term outcome data. Her story represents a broader pattern during the pandemic where experienced nurses and physicians who questioned the vaccination narrative faced professional punishment.

The article, featured on The Focal Points--a publication that has become a hub for independent medical analysis--underscores how credentialled professionals outside the institutional hierarchy were among the first to exercise precautionary skepticism. Allen's decision to prioritize her unborn child's safety over her career reflects the high personal cost paid by independent-minded healthcare workers who refused to defer to consensus when the evidentiary foundation appeared weak.

**III. FDA Officials ' Hidden Concerns: Johnson and Paul Disclosure**
Source: Just the News
Key Figures: Senator Ron Johnson (R-WI) and Senator Rand Paul (R-KY)

In an investigative report published by Just the News (justthenews.com), Senators Ron Johnson and Rand Paul released internal emails revealing that top FDA officials had expressed private concerns about COVID-19 vaccines that contradicted the agency's public assurances. The disclosed communications show that as early as March 2021, FDA analysts recognized that their VAERS surveillance system was "completely inadequate" and would "MASK significant safety signals"--yet these concerns were not communicated to the public.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3930f7c5-715a-4540-99e1-d851a4ceabe8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
According to the senators' findings, FDA officials presented analysis showing that an alternative surveillance system could produce unmasked safety data, but top agency leaders chose not to act on or disclose these limitations. Senator Johnson has described this as a "cover-up," noting that the FDA continued to issue blanket safety assurances while internally acknowledging that their monitoring infrastructure was incapable of detecting meaningful signals of harm.

The Just the News reporting represents independent journalism that circumvented the mainstream media's reluctance to cover vaccine safety controversies. The revelations from Johnson and Paul--drawn from whistleblowers and Freedom of Information Act requests--demonstrate that dissent existed even within regulatory agencies, but was suppressed by leadership committed to maintaining public confidence in mass vaccination campaigns at the expense of transparency.

**IV. "Does the PREP Act Shield Fauci and Others?"**
Author(s): Nicolas Hulscher, MPH, and contributors to The Focal Points (Epidemiologist; Foundation Administrator, The McCullough Foundation)
Key Figure Discussed: Dr. Anthony Fauci

Nicolas Hulscher's analysis in The Focal Points examines the Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness (PREP) Act of 2004 and its role in creating a comprehensive liability shield for government officials, pharmaceutical manufacturers, and healthcare administrators involved in COVID-19 countermeasures. Hulscher, an epidemiologist, argues that the PREP Act--extended repeatedly through HHS declarations--provides near-total immunity from civil liability for any harm caused by designated medical countermeasures, including COVID-19 vaccines.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8f96dff4-7606-4b6e-840b-459c7826daa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
https://rumble.com/v7bc96k-nicolas-hulscher-mph-champion-of-covid-19-vaccine-injury-syndrome-hlj-459.html

The article explores how this legal framework removes the normal market and legal incentives for safety that apply to virtually every other medical product. Under PREP Act protections, individuals harmed by COVID-19 vaccines cannot sue manufacturers in civil court, nor can they typically hold government officials like Dr. Anthony Fauci personally liable for policy decisions that led to injuries.

Hulscher's work at The Focal Point* positions the PREP Act within a broader legislative timeline--including the 2003 BioShield Act and the 1986 National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act--that progressively insulated vaccine makers and health officials from accountability. The article raises the concern that when decision-makers know they cannot be held liable for adverse outcomes, the incentive structure shifts toward speed and adoption rather than caution and rigorous safety verification.

**V. Synthesis: The Role of Independent Voices in Uncovering Suppressed Information**
What unites these four sources is their independence from the institutional structures that shaped COVID-19 public health policy. Jessica Rose operates outside academia and government; The Focal Points functions as an uncensored Substack publication rather than a peer-reviewed journal subject to editorial control; Just the News pursues investigative angles that legacy outlets avoided; and Nicolas Hulscher conducts epidemiological analysis through the McCullough Foundation rather than through CDC or NIH channels.

These independent researchers and journalists have documented a consistent pattern during the pandemic:

1\. Pregnancy and reproductive risks: Frontline professionals (like Adara Allen) and data analysts (like Jessica Rose) identified red flags in vaccinating pregnant women that institutional medicine dismissed or covered up.

2\. Suppressed safety signals: Senator Johnson's disclosures reveal that FDA officials knew their surveillance was inadequate yet maintained public confidence in safety monitoring they privately acknowledged as broken.

3\. Accountability avoidance: The PREP Act analysis demonstrates a pre-existing legal architecture designed to prevent, not facilitate, accountability for pandemic-era harms.

The establishment media, professional medical societies, and government health agencies have largely failed to engage substantively with these findings, preferring blanket characterizations of vaccine skeptics as "misinformation" rather than addressing the specific data and documents these independent voices have brought forward. The burden now falls on citizens, independent journalists, and courageous professionals to continue demanding the transparency and accountability that institutional channels have withheld.

If you had trusted the settled science of the day, here is how it would have gone:

1890s: you dose the baby with Bayer's new cough syrup, the non-addictive alternative to morphine, marketed for children. It was heroin. They named it after the German for heroic.

1900s: you rub calomel teething powder on your infant's gums. It is a mercury compound, and it leaves a generation with pink disease. Swollen, peeling hands and feet, screaming for months, and some of them died.

1910s: you cook in Crisco, launched by a soap and candle company, because cottonseed oil is modern and lard is what your mother used. The process that made it solid produced trans fat, banned outright a century later.

1920s: you drink Radithor, certified radioactive water, on prescription. Eben Byers took fourteen hundred bottles for his vitality. His jaw was removed in pieces and he was buried in a lead coffin.

1930s: a chemist dissolves a new sulfa drug in diethylene glycol, which is antifreeze. It kills 107 people, mostly children, and only then does America give the FDA power to demand safety testing.

1940s: your doctor lights a Camel in the surgery. More doctors smoke them than any other brand, and the advert runs in the Journal of the American Medical Association, which sold him the page.

1950s: DDT is sprayed over your kitchen, your garden and your children at school. The man who found its insecticidal properties has already been given a Nobel Prize.

1960s: your wife takes thalidomide for morning sickness because it is remarkably safe. More than ten thousand children are born with missing and shortened limbs.

1970s: the country puts down the butter and picks up the margarine, on the instruction of the American Heart Association. The fat everybody switched to was banned in 2015 as unsafe at any level.

1980s: the fat comes out of everything and sugar goes back in to make it edible. Obesity begins a climb it has never come off.

1990s: your father is prescribed OxyContin, because fewer than one per cent get addicted. The company later pleads guilty to criminal misbranding, and the overdose count runs into hundreds of thousands.

2000s: you take Vioxx for your knee. It is pulled in 2004, and the FDA's own safety officer estimates tens of thousands of excess heart attacks.

Not one of those was fringe. Every one had a professional body, a literature and a man in a white coat standing behind it. Nobody who followed that advice was stupid. They were obedient, to the most qualified people available. Settled is a word about money. It means the questions stopped being funded, so they stopped being asked. So which of today's instructions will your grandchildren read out in disbelief? The oil washed in hexane and built into every cell you own. The statin that blocks the pathway making your hormones, to prevent one heart attack per hundred people. The injection where a third of the loss is muscle. The infant formula built out of vegetable oil. All settled. None of it funded to be otherwise.

Friend, Wednesday night was our last quarterly deadline before Election Day, and I'm grateful to everyone who helped us get there. Some of you gave in the final hours. Others shared our emails with a friend or made their first donation of the cycle. That support carries us into the final stretch of this campaign, with ballots arriving in CA-45 mailboxes next week. September kept me busy in Washington and here at home, so I put together a few highlights from the month. If you only have a minute, a **[donation of $3](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140511976/650732876/439559405?refcode=em-10.2.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2NhNDUzZGQtODJiZS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CXGWTtYtMnxk6jLQu6pC3V4uz_vzBgCbz7uV37OKzmQ=)** keeps this work going through Election Day. | **[Donate](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140511977/650732877/439559405?refcode=em-10.2.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2NhNDUzZGQtODJiZS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CXGWTtYtMnxk6jLQu6pC3V4uz_vzBgCbz7uV37OKzmQ=)**

**I'm proud to share that the Orange County Business Council's BIZPAC has endorsed our campaign.** Orange County's business community has a long history of backing Republicans, and this isn't an endorsement a Democrat here gets handed. This month, a bipartisan bill to protect local businesses from foreign economic threats and intellectual property theft cleared committee. I co-sponsored the TIPS Act so restaurant, hotel, and salon workers can deduct their tips on their taxes, and I introduced the Housing Cost of Living Support for Tenants Act to give renters across Southern California some breathing room as rents keep climbing.
None of those ideas started in Washington. They came from conversations on doorsteps across CA-45, and our volunteers had plenty of them in September.

Our team in Fullerton spent the day making sure voters know their ballots are on the way (next week!).
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140511981/650732881/439559405?refcode=em-10.2.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2NhNDUzZGQtODJiZS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CXGWTtYtMnxk6jLQu6pC3V4uz_vzBgCbz7uV37OKzmQ=) _Volunteers in Cerritos_
And in Cerritos, another great group came out to keep those conversations going one door at a time. I'm grateful to every person who gave their time to engage our community.
All of that work needs resources behind it in the final stretch. Once ballots land in CA-45 mailboxes, voters can fill them out and send them back right away, so the window to reach people is shorter than it looks. If you live in the district, [**here's where to find everything you need to vote**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140511982/650732882/2080778256?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2NhNDUzZGQtODJiZS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CXGWTtYtMnxk6jLQu6pC3V4uz_vzBgCbz7uV37OKzmQ=&emci=c5a453dd-82be-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=cca453dd-82be-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=27336212).

| Letter from the Chair
---
| Friends,
For the first time in two decades, the President of the United States is returning to Grand Island.
It could not come at a more critical time as we are a month away from the most consequential midterm election of our lives.
Nebraskans have a stark choice in November - commonsense conservative policies versus Democrats' crazy leftwing agenda.
From eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security to making a historic investment in strengthening rural health care, President Trump and Senator Pete Ricketts have been delivering real results on the issues that matter most to Nebraskans.
Thanks to Republicans' Working Families Tax Cuts that provided the largest middle class tax cut in history, Nebraskans are keeping more of what they earn.
But that wouldn't have been the case if Democrat Dan Osborn had his way.
He has [said ](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0013oX71KaPFM5d5duHuvhJgUzB2jjEFXigy5DQTje8Ny-bp_IiUgvnJlSTdVjjWQBTQT1u4iBtgTEGxc398nYXC3w7NJb0I_k-ZqOIQvovtFS-S7F69uwb9wuFLfd9GITAFMrJpiZQgBE7owV4fH1yXpCf2bhzj3U_xcIV4l4JudWR8-KC-C1nbG3pbLcH1G7x&c=D0UEX-Jv5xsBnIaRH9RMw0dX8H08ck-TwWholqFx6WOmrtcIkk5yjw==&ch=1Y8wY-JW_IL0YvVtQmAJiNdi90WXTNCLrhQm1TntHa65pPhIA-IWPg==)he would have voted to raise taxes on every single Nebraskan by an average of $2,443 to fund an insane program giving healthcare to illegal aliens. That's just plain backwards.
While Democrats treat the heartland as flyover country, President Trump and Senator Ricketts have fought every single day for our farmers.
They passed key tax deductions allowing family farmers to write off much-needed investments in new equipment, tractors, and combines.
Republicans also eliminated the cruel death tax to ensure that family farms and ranches stay in the family for generations to come.
In addition to fighting for the long-term viability of family farms, Republicans are working to deliver a much-needed boost right now.
Senator Ricketts is leading the fight in Congress to deliver on President Trump's promise to make permanent year-round E-15. Unleashing American [biofuels](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0013oX71KaPFM5d5duHuvhJgUzB2jjEFXigy5DQTje8Ny-bp_IiUgvnJlSTdVjjWQBTpG26Cj8bfWvuCX7vXNTyN9UTI5iGRlfVa97rKqT21vOI6k8M_gjocatw1hlZBUF_zpmQRmHAX4zXoP2DTGQ0nHsGD28e3efAqkrU2m_KVosU4UM_2FXU_DPF6nMRkVhXbG9V_PBWmCQ445rNrd7xVTmooMe_I24n6iE2QPq1FxKMp_kJeuvG6lrjUlf2MTntuxjC6C6v9dzl_gx8sutD1g==&c=D0UEX-Jv5xsBnIaRH9RMw0dX8H08ck-TwWholqFx6WOmrtcIkk5yjw==&ch=1Y8wY-JW_IL0YvVtQmAJiNdi90WXTNCLrhQm1TntHa65pPhIA-IWPg==) not only provides a major boost to Nebraska farmers, but it also provides significant relief at the pump for consumers.
What does Democrat Dan Osborn have to say about our farmers and other hardworking Nebraskans?
That our lives "f*****g suck." That's not Nebraska nice.
While Dan Osborn slings mud and insults, Republicans continue to get things done for Nebraska.
Senator Ricketts worked with the Trump administration to provide $100 million to repair to the Gering-Fort Laramie Canal, which provides critical water infrastructure for farms and ranches in western Nebraska.
President Trump and Senator Ricketts also teamed up to create the $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program that awarded Nebraska $219 million this year to strengthen [health care](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0013oX71KaPFM5d5duHuvhJgUzB2jjEFXigy5DQTje8Ny-bp_IiUgvnJlSTdVjjWQBTjvzyU4jDbLmVDkFqcKV9qFqbtd-Vq1LJkYvlsCNu8EN-yzz7tpM6KsciJct_CyXV_fWDjmTDKVL7RQK17Sl_DmmB-VhMlwoAk2bAR_fVntnCvRSoEP-3Wg==&c=D0UEX-Jv5xsBnIaRH9RMw0dX8H08ck-TwWholqFx6WOmrtcIkk5yjw==&ch=1Y8wY-JW_IL0YvVtQmAJiNdi90WXTNCLrhQm1TntHa65pPhIA-IWPg==) in rural communities and ensure high-quality care for every single Nebraskan no matter your zip code.

Genuinely, from the bottom of my heart, thank you. When I won the runoff, the DC insiders laughed. The political establishment wrote us off. Dollar by dollar, you built something the establishment wasn’t expecting. A grassroots operation that has taken this race from a comfortable Ossoff win to a DEAD HEAT that has Chuck Schumer losing sleep every night. I am so deeply grateful, and I don’t ever want you to doubt that. We are within just a few points of Jon Ossoff, with Election Day bearing down on us fast. Every day between now and November 3rd is a day we either use to close that gap or hand back Ossoff and his Hollywood money machine. My team told me this morning they have set a October 6th fundraising goal of $75,000. This will help us secure another ad purchase that WILL change the tides in this race. Dear Friends,Have you seen our newest campaign [ad](https://us.list-manage.com/_JFPjk3KeNe?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)? [[Watch here](https://us.list-manage.com/12NcMzgImm8?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)]The ad highlights several recent legislative victories, including:✅ Tax relief for Arizona families✅ Eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and retirement income✅ Expanding housing opportunities✅ Protecting Arizona's water futureI can't fix the dysfunction in Washington, DC, but I can continue fighting to solve problems here in Arizona.
Over the past few weeks, I've been traveling throughout Legislative District 2, meeting with voters, attending community events, and hearing directly from families about the issues that matter most: affordability, education, public safety, and opportunity.
Here's a quick update on what I've been working on.🎓 ESA Program Continues to GrowI recently met with Arizona ESA leadership to discuss the continued growth of the Empowerment Scholarship Account program.Today, more than 107,000 Arizona students are utilizing ESAs to access educational opportunities that best meet their needs. We discussed enrollment trends, program operations, and efforts to ensure families continue receiving timely support.School choice empowers parents, and I remain committed to protecting educational freedom for Arizona families.
🏛️ Policy Fellowship Success: Restoring the American Dream by Building a National Housing Opportunity MovementI recently completed the final sessions of my Club for Growth Foundation Policy Fellowship, with seminars held in Boston and Philadelphia as part of America’s upcoming 250th anniversary celebration.Even better, my team's policy proposal won a “Shark Tank-style” competition focused on one of the biggest challenges facing families today: housing affordability and restoring the American Dream. For generations, the American Dream meant working hard, saving money, buying a home, and building a better future.Today, that dream is slipping further out of reach for many young families.Teachers, nurses, first responders, veterans, and working families are increasingly priced out of the communities they love. As the mother of two young adults, this issue is deeply personal to me.That's why housing affordability has been one of my top priorities at the Arizona Capitol.Housing is about more than buildings.It's about opportunity.The opportunity to own a home. The opportunity to build wealth. The opportunity to raise a family. The opportunity to achieve the American Dream.To make that possible again, we must restore the freedom to build.Our winning fellowship proposal would create a nationwide coalition of lawmakers, local leaders, builders, employers, economists, housing advocates, and citizens committed to expanding housing opportunities.The goal is simple:• Share successful reforms• Educate policymakers• Increase housing supply• Improve affordability• Help more families achieve homeownershipFuture homeowners deserve a voice, too.
✅ Results DeliveredDuring a recent address to our local Republican committee, I highlighted a few accomplishments from my three years in the State Senate:• Protected children through reforms to family court reunification practices• Expanded protections for domestic violence victims• Created Arizona's Independent Correctional Oversight Office• Passed Jerry's Law to strengthen animal cruelty protections• Strengthened protections for victims of sexual violence• Improved reporting requirements for missing and kidnapped children• Increased accountability in assisted living referral services• Modernized education and licensing regulations• Advanced election integrity reforms through Proposition 144When I was appointed in 2023 and elected in 2024, I promised to fight for Arizona families and deliver results. That's exactly what I've done.
🏘️ Housing Town HallOn Wednesday morning, I participated in a housing affordability town hall alongside nonprofit leaders, business leaders, and young adults hoping to someday achieve homeownership at one of Maricopa County’s community colleges.The message was clear: Arizona needs more attainable housing options.Once I am re-elected, I will continue working with stakeholders across the state to advance practical solutions that increase housing supply and keep the American Dream within reach for the next generation.
📢 Join UsThere is still more work to do.We must make Arizona more affordable. We must protect public safety. We must stand with victims. We must defend educational freedom. And we must create more opportunities for families to thrive.Together, we've made real progress.Together, we'll keep Arizona moving forward.Let's win this in November! 🇺🇸Sincerely,Shawnna

Here’s the rundown.
September was our busiest and best month yet.
More doors knocked. More relationships built. More ballots chased. More momentum than we’ve **_ever had in a single month_**.
And because of that success, we’ve burned through our financial resources faster than planned.
**[We _cannot_ run out of money to keep ballot chasers on the ground at the worst possible time in this election cycle.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMTd9AAwAAAAAA0uIhjMYW_Thd52MarWX7Jk26_bb6SLpkcg2bIe7_sC8ZzEj_u2SpCfhhq6wXDyBV1OWUCAgQiqBrEdoPwFW6-uOavQHGJF3nUZde4Kg_w)**

You’re one of Turning Point’s most dedicated supporters. When the rest of the list goes quiet, folks like you step up.
