**CONCORD, N.H.** — Today, Pete Buttigieg will hold a rally in New Hampshire. Ahead of the event, New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement:“Democrats hate New Hampshire, and they sent Pete Buttigieg to our state to try to make up for taking the First-in-the-Nation primary away from us,” **said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “Pete is not the moderate the left wants Granite Staters to believe he is. He supports taxpayer-funded healthcare for illegal aliens, abolishing the Electoral College, and packing the Supreme Court. We also cannot forget his failed record as Transportation Secretary, where he spent $80 billion on DEI grants while air traffic control modernization fell behind. His arrival in New Hampshire is nothing to celebrate.”“Even worse, he is campaigning alongside Opioid Lobbyist Cinde Warmington, Washington insider Stefany Shaheen, and Corrupt Chris Pappas. The fact that they are all supporting an Opioid Lobbyist shows just how desperate and out of touch the Democratic Party has become with Granite Staters.”

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life 's mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he's determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe's entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.
Upcoming events
As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Pittsburgh%20School%20board%20forum%208.5x11.png]
Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students.
Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader.
With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color.

Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot.
Your vote shapes our justice system!
Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager
Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms.

[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/7237344C447445787878394747342B75584E47375A57552F745265427662334B544A4A36505A58657A5871474B7A5A6E53705571424758325657365969365747/editor_images/WCM%20logo.JPG] #CourtsMatter
This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/DelCo_2.png] We are hiring!
Let's provide civic education together!
We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania.
Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote!
Positions start at $20 an hour.
Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org]
EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org]
News You Can Use
There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
* New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pittsburgh-mayor-election-2025-candidates-quiz]
* Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections/assistant/]
* Everything you need to know about mail voting [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-mail-ballot-how-to-request-fill-out-return] , becoming a poll worker [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide]
* Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pennsylvania-primary-election-day-2025-voter-information-registration]
* Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-commonwealth-superior-court-candidates] , vetting judicial candidates [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-candidate-vetting-guide]
* Guides to State College school board [https://www.spotlightpa.org/statecollege/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-state-college-school-board-anderson-huff-barlow-black-desmarais-mcternan-sogor] , Reading City Council president [https://www.spotlightpa.org/berks/2025/04/reading-city-council-president-primary-election-2025]
* Guides to voting as a college student [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-college-student-voting-guide]
En Español
* Guía para votar por correo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pensilvania-elecciones-primarias-2025-votar-correo-como-llenar] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/reading-concejo-municipal-primarias-elecciones-2025]
* Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-primarias-elecciones-2025-votar-informacion] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-elecciones-2025-como-convertirse-trabajador-electoral]
2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:

clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed. The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error. Upcoming events As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls. [] Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students. Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader. With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color. When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] [] Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot. Your vote shapes our justice system! Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms. When: Monday, May 12, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] Social Media of the Week [] The deadline to request your mail-in ballot for the primary election is May 13th at 5PM. Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [] The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests. In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. _Speaking with members of the Rocky Mountain Farmers Union — the folks who feed us._ I was grateful for their vote of confidence. And I was grateful to have begun earning it by listening and learning from them in town hall meetings, as we were preparing to fight back against the Kroger/Albertson’s proposed supermarket mega-merger (which ultimately didn’t go through, thanks in part to our work together). What I learned from Colorado’s farmers at those town halls echoed as we discussed SNAP, supply chains, local food distribution, water, and thinking about food as a system in that backyard. We also spoke about the mental health of rural Coloradans, which reminded me of my friend and rural mental health leader JC Carrica’s question: **“Do you look after your neighbor as close as your crop or herd?”** **[Folks, as your next governor, I’ll do whatever I can to help Coloradans in farming, ranching, and agriculture answer that question with a resounding “yes” — because I believe all of us need all of us. subject: I am worried...

body:
| Hello,
I am worried.

I think about the lengths Donald Trump will go to hold on to power and I am terrified about what happens if we do not take back control of Congress.

We're talking about a man who tried to light democracy on fire when he lost the election. He tried to rig the next election before the first vote was cast with redistricting ploys. There is no telling what he will try to do with mail-in ballots and after votes are counted.

Trump will do A-N-Y-T-H-I-N-G

That is why I am reaching out to ask for your help.

Richard Pan is one of the "tipping point" races for control of the House. Of course, Republicans know that too. That is why they are spending a considerable amount of money to defeat him.

Richard is one of these seats we can flip because we passed the Election Rigging Response Act in California and he needs our help NOW.

So if you are someone who wants to make strategically wise doations to help Democrats win this November, there may be no wiser place to donate today than Richard Pan's campaign for Congress in California.

**[Please use this link to contribute to Richard Pan's campaign for Congress today. Do it before the final FEC deadline of the campaign ends. His average online donation is around $30. We’ve set some very ambitious goals for this final month, and we have to hit them if we are going to win. There is no room for error in a district as competitive as NY-17. We’ve managed to close the gap with him significantly, thanks to this grassroots team. And brand new polling shows us with a slim lead. But NY-17 is on track to be the most expensive and competitive race in the country. We can’t afford to take our foot off the gas for a moment.
We are going to be outspent. We do not need to match Republicans dollar-for-dollar, but our team needs to be able to field on-the-ground volunteers and push back against their TV ads.
I come from a blue-collar family. After West Point, I spent 16 years in the Army, I did six tours overseas, and was the Director for Counterterrorism at the White House.
Asking for money doesn't come naturally to me. But I have to, if we’re going to meet these October goals.
This is a grassroots campaign – a huge amount of our budget every month comes from donations of just $10, $5, even $1. So when you see me and my team out there, please know: We’re only able to do so because of the response to emails like this one.

Florida's limestone is an immense, unseen expanse--
a restless ocean coursing through porous stone beneath our feet.
Normally, water reaches these depths --
a slow, rhythmic filtration through the hidden realm.
But an injection well bypasses that patience entirely.
It creates an engineered pathway, forcing pre-treated leachate
directly into the deep geological formations below.
While treatment is a mere moment in a lab,
geology is measured in pressures and epochs.
We are no longer simply receiving what falls;
we are deliberately injecting material into these silent veins,
trusting safeguards to contain the unknown.
**What we cannot see still has consequences.
What we decide today does not end with us.**
Our water.
Our ground.
Our progeny.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**

Friend,

Small business owners are the backbone of Arkansas. Their shops fill street corners with opportunities and communities that keep our economy strong.

That’s why I’m honored to share that the National Federation of Independent Businesses (NFIB) has officially endorsed our campaign for re-election to the U.S. Senate.

The NFIB awarded me a 100% Voting Record because I’ve consistently fought to protect Arkansas from overregulation and higher taxes. I fought to make the small business tax deduction **permanent** in the Working Families Tax Cut because decisions like these are what keep hard-working families afloat.

**But our opponent, Hallie Shoffner, wants to take Arkansas in a completely different direction.**

She’s called for a national energy tax and opposed tax cuts that allow small business owners to reinvest in their workers and local communities. **Her agenda would mean heavier burdens and fewer opportunities for working families.**

We cannot let anti-business policies take root in Arkansas.

Today, I’m humbly asking for your support so I can keep spreading this message. Standing up for free enterprise means standing up for the hard-working Americans who make our communities thrive.

For most of the last decade, if you told someone Democrats could win the North Carolina House, they'd look at you like you'd lost your mind. Republican gerrymandering [made it virtually impossible](https://substack.com/redirect/1b5e1908-9d75-468c-823d-8c5617206f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
This year, _impossible_ looks a whole lot more like **possible**. Here's why.
#### **Republicans just cut bait on Michael Whatley**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/24def58e-2146-45f3-9840-a351d16b59dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A few hours ago the top Republican super PAC for Senate races [canceled all of its remaining ads in North Carolina](https://substack.com/redirect/24def58e-2146-45f3-9840-a351d16b59dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and moved the money to Kansas. That's tens of millions of dollars. Whatley's own super PAC had already pulled ads too.
That's great news for Roy Cooper. But it matters even more down the ballot.
A big-money Senate race is what fires up MAGA voters and gets them to the polls. When national Republicans walk away from the top of the ticket, the Republicans running in close state House races lose that air cover. National Republicans would have spent millions turning out MAGA voters for Whatley - that turnout money leaves as well. Downballot Republicans are now on their own and this becomes the kind of year when the seats that "lean Republican" can flip.
#### **Where things stand**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7066e84b-78e2-486d-b36f-84a64be4f836?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Republicans hold 71 of the 120 seats in the NC House. It takes 61 to win a majority.
Using the Civitas Partisan Index, which comes from the conservative John Locke Foundation, Democrats start with 47 seats that lean our way. To get to 61, we have to hold those, sweep the seven toss-up districts, and [then win seven of the 15 seats](https://substack.com/redirect/1b5e1908-9d75-468c-823d-8c5617206f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that lean Republican.
That's a tall order. But it's not crazy anymore.
#### **What a +10 year would mean**
Right now, polling averages have Democrats [up about 8 points](https://substack.com/redirect/137ab643-2391-4b9e-93ca-4afdc7eed862?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nationally on the generic ballot. Some recent polls have it even higher. [Emerson](https://substack.com/redirect/e831d236-17d6-403e-8520-95e49b580aaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has us up 11. [Marist ](https://substack.com/redirect/89e21266-e3c2-4201-8b12-9c961146f714?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)has us up 12.
Here's why that matters. [Carolina Forward crunched the numbers](https://substack.com/redirect/ecb599c6-35f0-4cf7-97bf-0c6bea6dc602?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and found Democrats would need to do about 5 to 6 points better statewide than we did in 2024 to win the NC House. In 2024, Republicans won the national House vote by about 2.6 points.
So a 10-point Democratic lead nationally would be a swing of more than 12 points from 2024. That's about double what we'd need.
Now, a big caveat. National polls don't line up perfectly with North Carolina, and gerrymandered districts are built to soak up waves. But if anything close to a +10 year shows up here, the House majority in the NC General Assembly is in reach.
#### **Why flipping the House matters**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9bdfa0c3-995f-41a7-8553-30c81e0b2e01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I served in the state Senate. I know what it's like when Republicans run everything and don't have to listen to Democrats.
The biggest one for me is redistricting. In North Carolina, the legislature draws the maps and the governor can't veto them. That's how Republicans redrew the congressional map in 2023 and flipped three seats in 2024, including mine. It's how they redrew it again last fall to go after Don Davis in the 1st District.
With a Democratic House, that stops. Every map, every budget and every bill comes from House Democrats. That means a real seat at the table for public schools, for the cost of living, and for everything else Republicans have been deciding on their own. It means a sea change for voting right and women's reproductive health rights.
#### **Come join me**
That's why I'm hosting [a fundraiser for House Democratic Leader Robert Reives](https://substack.com/redirect/21e8c6fc-2490-4a21-a1de-e94925e2a998?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday October 22nd in Cary.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c5a7872b-48c5-4d81-b02e-69cf05b517bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Robert has led the House Democrats since 2021, and I'd sure like to call him our next Speaker of the House.
Every dollar goes to Robert Reives. If you can make it, I'd love to see you here in Cary. If you can't make it, please [chip in for the effort](https://substack.com/redirect/21e8c6fc-2490-4a21-a1de-e94925e2a998?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[RSVP OR DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/21e8c6fc-2490-4a21-a1de-e94925e2a998?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For years, flipping the NC House was a long shot. This year, there's a real shot. Let's take it.

clean_body: Now we've got a real shot to flip the NC House. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Now we've got a real shot to flip the NC House. | | | Oct 2 | | | | | | | | | | | | For most of the last decade, if you told someone Democrats could win the North Carolina House, they'd look at you like you'd lost your mind. Republican gerrymandering . This year, impossible looks a whole lot more like possible. Here's why. Republicans just cut bait on Michael Whatley | | ---|---|--- A few hours ago the top Republican super PAC for Senate races and moved the money to Kansas. That's tens of millions of dollars. Whatley's own super PAC had already pulled ads too. That's great news for Roy Cooper. But it matters even more down the ballot. A big-money Senate race is what fires up MAGA voters and gets them to the polls. When national Republicans walk away from the top of the ticket, the Republicans running in close state House races lose that air cover. National Republicans would have spent millions turning out MAGA voters for Whatley - that turnout money leaves as well. Downballot Republicans are now on their own and this becomes the kind of year when the seats that "lean Republican" can flip. Where things stand | | ---|---|--- Republicans hold 71 of the 120 seats in the NC House. It takes 61 to win a majority. Using the Civitas Partisan Index, which comes from the conservative John Locke Foundation, Democrats start with 47 seats that lean our way. To get to 61, we have to hold those, sweep the seven toss-up districts, and that lean Republican. That's a tall order. But it's not crazy anymore. What a +10 year would mean Right now, polling averages have Democrats nationally on the generic ballot. Some recent polls have it even higher. has us up 11. us up 12. Here's why that matters. and found Democrats would need to do about 5 to 6 points better statewide than we did in 2024 to win the NC House. In 2024, Republicans won the national House vote by about 2.6 points. So a 10-point Democratic lead nationally would be a swing of more than 12 points from 2024. That's about double what we'd need. Now, a big caveat. National polls don't line up perfectly with North Carolina, and gerrymandered districts are built to soak up waves. But if anything close to a +10 year shows up here, the House majority in the NC General Assembly is in reach. Why flipping the House matters | | ---|---|--- I served in the state Senate. I know what it's like when Republicans run everything and don't have to listen to Democrats. The biggest one for me is redistricting. In North Carolina, the legislature draws the maps and the governor can't veto them. That's how Republicans redrew the congressional map in 2023 and flipped three seats in 2024, including mine. It's how they redrew it again last fall to go after Don Davis in the 1st District. With a Democratic House, that stops. Every map, every budget and every bill comes from House Democrats. That means a real seat at the table for public schools, for the cost of living, and for everything else Republicans have been deciding on their own. It means a sea change for voting right and women's reproductive health rights. Come join me That's why I'm hosting on Thursday October 22nd in Cary. | | ---|---|--- Robert has led the House Democrats since 2021, and I'd sure like to call him our next Speaker of the House. Every dollar goes to Robert Reives. If you can make it, I'd love to see you here in Cary. If you can't make it, please . For years, flipping the NC House was a long shot. This year, there's a real shot. Let's take it. Wiley ? PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY WILEY FOR WAKE ? Democracy is on the ballot. Join the fight at . | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Wiley for Wake P.O. # [The October Fed rate hike bet just broke, down from 69% to 16%](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Traders **[marked an October rate increase as a long shot](https://substack.com/redirect/dc827de5-e2bf-4274-b5ff-b07a8ccafead?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after employers added 29,000 jobs in September, far short of forecasts for a gain above 80,000.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Futures price a hold:** CME FedWatch put a quarter-point October hike at 17%, down from close to 36% a week earlier.
* **Kalshi odds tumble:** The prediction market showed an 18% chance of an October increase, from almost 70% a week ago.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/543babd6-f707-4eda-8958-93af887e22d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **December hike remains:** FedWatch still priced a December increase above 75%, with Kalshi at 65%. The next decision is Oct. 28, after a September hike.
* **Cooler prices already:** Core prices rose 3% in August, under a 3.3% consensus. Vanguard economist Adam Schickling said the report "strengthens the case for the Federal Reserve to remain patient."

# [The 10-year Treasury yield just slid to 5.18% on a jobs miss](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Treasury **[yields fell Friday after a soft September payrolls report](https://substack.com/redirect/afd9cc2d-62bb-43fa-ab2e-1c4d55d4c3a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** eased a bond selloff that **[had pushed the 10-year to its highest level since 2002.](https://substack.com/redirect/475b55b9-0420-4446-9cfb-f501b8aec1c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Benchmark yields retreat:** The 10-year fell nearly 6 basis points to 5.18%. The 30-year slipped 3 basis points to 5.57%, and the 2-year fell 6 basis points to 4.73%.
* **Payrolls miss badly:** Employers added 29,000 jobs. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. Dow Jones had expected 84,000 jobs and a steady jobless rate. August was revised to a 133,000 gain.
* **October hold priced:** FedWatch showed an 84% chance of an October hold. Lindsay Rosner of Goldman kept a December hike as the base case, though energy prices could still force action this month.
* **Thursday peak context:** Yahoo put Thursday's 10-year high at 5.342% and the 30-year at 5.683%, the richest in more than two decades.

# [Brent Crude slips under $100 as Europe eyes its reserves](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Oil fell Friday after a report that **[EU states were weighing a French plan to release diesel reserves,](https://substack.com/redirect/8e1a457d-a6d9-494e-82e7-283764d23414?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** pulling Brent back under $100 a barrel.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Prices back under $100:** December Brent fell 2.6% to $99.65 and November WTI dropped 4% to $89.11, after a higher settle on a report of a third U.S. carrier group plus 2,000 Marines.
* **French 50 million plan:** One unnamed source told Reuters France wants EU nations to release 50 million barrels of diesel and IEA members to release 50 million of crude.
* **Bessent presses Europe:** EU crisis talks follow a Thursday post from Scott Bessent urging partners to "accelerate delivery on their existing commitments" and not leave U.S. farmers and truckers "carrying the burden."
* **Ban talk cools:** Trump appeared to ease off a diesel export ban earlier this week after Hormuz crude exports picked up. The U.S. supplied about half of EU diesel imports in August.

# [Wall Street is syndicating $60 billion of AI chip debt](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Banks are preparing to syndicate **[$60 billion in fresh AI-chip debt meant to help Anthropic and other buyers,](https://substack.com/redirect/b3f91ea2-6c50-49be-82fd-2b090d0157f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** people familiar with the still-unannounced package told Bloomberg.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Senior slice goes out:** Banks are set to circulate letters for a $42 billion Class A senior-secured tranche. The deal has not been announced, and Broadcom declined to comment.
* **Blackstone takes junior:** Blackstone is leading an $18 billion Class B junior piece, committing $9 billion from various funds and planning to syndicate the rest.
* **Weeks in the making:** People familiar with the talks said the financing, shaped over weeks, would help Anthropic and others obtain chips and gear. Broadcom is pushing to sell more equipment against Nvidia.
* **Debt pile keeps growing:** The package adds to hundreds of billions already borrowed for AI infrastructure. In August, Nvidia and six finance firms, including Blackstone, said they would mobilize more than $500 billion.

---|---|---
* **Buy call unchanged:** Moore kept an overweight rating and a $300 target, saying Nvidia looks "well positioned, with a very undemanding valuation."
* **Customers beyond labs:** Management told him demand runs beyond hyperscale data-center operators and frontier AI labs, and that agentic AI is a plus for both CPUs and GPUs.
* **Buy zone still messy:** IBD charts show an Aug. 27 breakout from a cup-with-handle at 227.92. The stock has since moved in and out of that zone, and traded at 235.96 before the open.
* **Buyback just enlarged:** Monday's board added $150 billion, leaving $235 billion to finish by the end of fiscal 2028. The top-pick label, awarded in March, was dropped six months later.

# [Citi lifts Strategy to $240 as Bitcoin clears $87,000](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bitcoin **[rose above $87,000 Friday](https://substack.com/redirect/8c930214-46a6-4e58-8aa2-bbe2c726c6b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8c930214-46a6-4e58-8aa2-bbe2c726c6b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)after a Fed official urged patience on further rate increases, before retreating to $85,000 lifting Strategy and prompting Citi to nearly double its target to $240.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

# [Amazon locks 20 years of Maryland nuclear power for AI](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Amazon **[agreed to take 690 megawatts from Maryland's Calvert Cliffs for 20 years,](https://substack.com/redirect/bfd583ca-acf5-41b6-aaf2-bb50b99b98af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a Constellation pact that backs more than $3 billion in infrastructure and a later expansion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Expansion dated 2030:** The companies said Wednesday the contract supports about 190 megawatts of new capacity expected online between 2030 and 2032.
* **Power stays on grid:** Output will keep feeding the 13-state PJM system rather than a private line to Amazon. A separate retail supply deal covers Amazon sites across that market.
* **Licenses run to 2036:** Constellation will seek another 20 years on reactors licensed through 2034 and 2036. The site can produce 1,790 megawatts, equal to more than 1.3 million homes.
* **Prior nuclear checks:** Amazon already invested $500 million in X-energy and has an Energy Northwest small-reactor deal in Washington.

# [OpenAI fires three safety researchers over leaked data](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI removed three safety researchers after finding they mishandled sensitive company information, **[the Wall Street Journal reported,](https://substack.com/redirect/f507ccb5-9994-43af-a145-8aa9ef844420?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the same stretch the lab held back a new model.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4336c1-7933-4406-ac90-a40cec75f7e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Company confirms exits:** A spokesperson said OpenAI had "parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," and that an investigation confirmed mishandling outside set procedures.
* **Outside group alleged:** Journal sources said the three were on the safety team and shared confidential material with a third-party AI safety organization. Fox said it had asked the company for comment.
* **Astra model held back:** Fox confirmed earlier this week that safety leaders chose not to release GPT-6.1 Astra. Saachi Jain, head of safety systems, said it improved on laziness but "didn't quite meet the bar in terms of staying within scope and authorization."
* **Six misaligned cases:** OpenAI has also listed six cases of models writing their own instructions, hiding mistakes in summaries, inventing details with exposed API keys, uploading files so they could cite them, and agents contacting each other without approval.

body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Friend,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.
---

We're not sitting around waiting on November and hoping everything falls our way. Our teams are already on the ground in these three states, doing the actual work. Knocking doors. Registering voters. Chasing down every conservative ballot until it's counted. Clipboard and tennis shoes work, the kind that doesn't trend online but wins elections. We proved this model in 2024. We ran the most sophisticated ballot-chasing operation the Right has ever put together, and we won every single state where we ran it. 10 for 10. Now we're doing it again, in the three states that decide everything this time. ${Recipient.FirstName}, this is how you can help us win this November. **Every dollar you send fuels the machine we're building in Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire right now. clean_body: There are so many ways to get involved over the next few weeks!| | | | | | | Dear Peter, Election season is in full swing! Exciting times come with exciting events, and there are so many ways to get involved over the next few weeks. Whether you have a few hours on a Saturday or a full weekend to give, there are endless options for you. Here's what's coming up: Weekend Canvasses Every weekend between now and November 3, Team Massachusetts is hosting coordinated canvasses in communities near you. Conversations at the door are one of the most effective ways to reach voters, and this is the perfect opportunity to do your part. No experience is needed. We pair first-timers with seasoned volunteers, walk you through what to say, and give you everything you need to hit the ground running. Come for a shift, or stay for the whole day. | | | | | | Annual Chinatown Banquet: October 20 Lastly, our annual Chinatown Banquet is on October 20. We look forward to this fundraiser every year, and it's always a highlight of the season: great food, great company, and a chance to celebrate the work we've done together while powering the work to come. Every ticket supports electing Democrats across the Commonwealth. | | | = | | | Make the Most of the Final Stretch With the election less than five weeks away, we can't take our foot off the gas. Every door knocked, every voter reached, and every dollar raised between now and Election Day counts. We hope you make the most of this election season and join us for these wonderful events. Folks, there’s no other way to say it: **We’re being outspent 168 to 1.**
That’s a serious gap, and if we don’t work together to close it ASAP, undecided voters may not hear from us before they go to cast their ballot.
**[This is a make-or-break moment for our campaign. Please, rush a donation of $5 or any amount to help us catch up before it’s too late.](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261002_1_ak.DLhpPo&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-996&t=3&akid=1005%2E127862%2EGcmXO1)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261002_1_ak.DLhpPo&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-996&t=4&akid=1005%2E127862%2EGcmXO1)**
Unlike Lombardo, I don’t have a Rolodex of billionaire donors I can call and ask for a favor. I have you and other members of our grassroots team to count on.
I wouldn’t have it any other way, but that doesn’t change the fact that our fundraising pace isn’t where it should be.
This race is a total toss-up. Election forecasters say it, and I can feel it on the ground. **Truly, the factor that will matter most in determining who wins this is who can break through the noise and get their message across to as many Nevadans as possible.**
That requires ample resources, and right now, Lombardo is outmatching us.
We still have time to bounce back, but that window is closing quickly. **[Help us get back in the fight by chipping in $5 or whatever you can afford today:](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261002_1_ak.DLhpPo&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-996&t=5&akid=1005%2E127862%2EGcmXO1)**

Thanks so much,
Aaron

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Shove it with your culture wars
body:
This shouldn’t be about culture wars. This should be about you.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
I recently spoke with Dasha Burns on Politico’s _The Conversation,_ and I wanted to make sure you heard about it here too.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261002_2_culture.96C2co&refcode=em20261002-2308&amount=5&t=1&akid=2308%2E299639%2EeMjo7b)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261002_2_culture.96C2co&refcode=em20261002-2308&amount=5&t=2&akid=2308%2E299639%2EeMjo7b)
Instead of taking the GOP bait on various culture wars, I am focused solely on delivering for Texans and making life easier for working families.
Republicans have built their campaigns around creating culture wars and ragebait instead of focusing on plausible solutions to the issues voters care most about.
Instead, we should be focusing on how to help the everyday struggles of working people, and what we can do right away to help ease these struggles.
With the cost of living rising everywhere, Texans are tired of hearing about what needs to change. They’re looking for leaders who are ready to fight for them.
Abbott has proven that he answers to his donors — who are corporations and tech billionaires.
I’m also ready to answer to my donors — you. A movement of grassroots support that is ready for change in Texas.
That’s why, with this campaign, I vowed to go back to the basics: What’s most important to Texans? And what can we do to help?
People are tired of hating each other — we have strayed too far from community. **If we don’t come together, then we all lose.**
Are you with us, Peter?
**[Pitch in $5 or whatever you can today to help continue powering this grassroots movement and beat Greg Abbott in November.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261002_2_culture.96C2co&refcode=em20261002-2308&amount=5&t=3&akid=2308%2E299639%2EeMjo7b)**

Thank you,
Gina

name: Adam at The Dads Initiative
subject: Sign Our Open Letter from Dads on the Cornell Seven
body:
The Cornell Seven case demands we all do better. Sign our Open Letter from Dads.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/84dc80907346/the-dads-initiatives-second-show-cart-talk-7232572?e=7e921d898f)
---
| | | | Hi Peter,
_A note before you read: this email discusses sexual assault._ I'm writing to you today not just as the director of The Dads Initiative, but as a dad.
If you’ve seen the news about the Cornell Seven case, I’m sure you’re as horrified as I am.
If you’re not familiar: a young woman alleged she was drugged and sexually assaulted by seven fraternity members at a party on Cornell's campus. The story is unbearably awful. Even worse, though the assault was reported in 2024, no charges have yet been brought in the case. [You can read more about the case here. ](https://us.list-manage.com/kqpRBruXvIS?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)
As a dad raising a young son, I can’t help but think about how we, as a society, are failing. It’s on us, as dads, to speak up, to model a better manhood, and to demand more.
---
**So that’s why we’ve written an Open Letter from Dads on the Cornell Seven, and I’m asking you to add your name.**
| [Sign the Open Letter](https://us.list-manage.com/v_9hGhC_e4Q?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)
---
| |

And if this matters to you, forward this to another dad. The more of us who sign, the more men and boys will hear it.
Best,Adam

**Democrats have a snowball’s chance in hell of retaking the U.S. Senate majority this fall without flipping North Carolina’s red seat blue.**
Ain’t nobody’s done that since 2008, and right now, the GOP is flooding beaucoup bucks into NC to keep it that way. That’s ‘cause having a proven winner like two-term former Governor Roy Cooper as the Democratic nominee is our best chance of flipping any of the four seats we need.
Roy can’t overcome the full force of the GOP’s dark-money machine on his own, **[so if you’re my kind of Democrat – the kind who believes our #1 mission is to take back the Senate from Trump’s far-right flunkies – then I’mma need you to get off your derrière and pitch in $15 split between Cooper Victory Fund and State Democrats Committee ASAP.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/108764?refcode=em20261002-10969&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10969%2E614464%2EVNh_6G)**

name: Jahana Hayes
subject: 6 million moms and kids are missing out
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Jahana Hayes
body:
Add your name as a citizen cosponsor of the WIC for Kids Act. | | Friend, nearly 6 million mothers and children are eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) **but are not receiving the benefits they qualify for.** WIC is one of the most effective investments we can make in families. By providing healthy foods, personalized nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals to other services, WIC leads to healthier infants, more nutritious diets, and stronger families. _Yet only about half of eligible families participate._ **That is why I introduced the WIC for Kids Act, legislation that removes unnecessary barriers keeping eligible families from accessing the nutrition children need for healthy early development.** _[**Will you add your name as a citizen cosponsor to show elected officials that the public wants every eligible family connected to WIC?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140520670/650754486/771589941?refcode=AU_JH_EG_GEN_GEN_IN_20261002_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82ODk4NiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTdjOTk5Mi04ZmJlLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dX5hjzolQVkKs5o4QqOvZg39gfIgTKORQuIF_VjfwfY=&emci=a37c9992-8fbe-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=b17c9992-8fbe-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=15529135)_ | [SIGN THE PETITION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140520671/650754487/771589941?refcode=AU_JH_EG_GEN_GEN_IN_20261002_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82ODk4NiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTdjOTk5Mi04ZmJlLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dX5hjzolQVkKs5o4QqOvZg39gfIgTKORQuIF_VjfwfY=&emci=a37c9992-8fbe-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=b17c9992-8fbe-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=15529135)

Families who already qualify through one program should not have to fight through red tape to get help feeding their kids.
**The WIC for Kids Act will:**
* **Grant automatic WIC eligibility** to families already participating in programs like SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP, and Head Start.
* Help align certification periods **so families can consolidate appointments and stay enrolled.**
* **Direct states to include plans** for serving kinship families.

clean_body: Add your name as a citizen cosponsor of the WIC for Kids Act. | | Friend, nearly 6 million mothers and children are eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) but are not receiving the benefits they qualify for. WIC is one of the most effective investments we can make in families. By providing healthy foods, personalized nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals to other services, WIC leads to healthier infants, more nutritious diets, and stronger families. Yet only about half of eligible families participate. That is why I introduced the WIC for Kids Act, legislation that removes unnecessary barriers keeping eligible families from accessing the nutrition children need for healthy early development. | Families who already qualify through one program should not have to fight through red tape to get help feeding their kids. The WIC for Kids Act will: Grant automatic WIC eligibility to families already participating in programs like SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP, and Head Start. Help align certification periods so families can consolidate appointments and stay enrolled. Direct states to include plans for serving kinship families. The National WIC Association, the Food Research and Action Center, Connecticut Foodshare, and other advocates working to end hunger endorse this bill. name: Roy Cooper
subject: What would you do?
body:
Go with me for a moment...
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1566&source=&t=1&akid=4122%2E124072%2EW4zYRt) | | | |
---
Hey, Peter. It’s me again.
I know we’ve been in your inbox a lot lately. You’re probably sick of getting asked to donate so frequently, and I get it – [**_but before I ask you to chip in one last time today_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1566&amount=5&t=8&akid=4122%2E124072%2EW4zYRt), I just want to ask you to put yourself in my shoes:
What would _you_ do if you were a Democrat running for U.S. Senate in a state that President Trump swept all three times?
What would _you_ do if the Senate majority was hinging on you flipping that battleground seat blue for the first time since 2008?
What would _you_ do, as a state-level public servant, knowing that billionaires – **including the President of the United States** – would spare no expense and say whatever it took to ensure your defeat?
What would _you_ do if you saw your lead in the polls shrinking by the day, because that’s what always happens in NC – _remember the first time you ran for Governor back in 2016?_
Wouldn’t you turn to the folks you’ve been able to count on for help, if you were in my position? Because now more than ever, that’s what I need from every person reading this email tonight.
[**_So if _and only if_ you’ve got room in your budget for it, Peter, will you please chip in $5, or any amount now to my grassroots campaign tonight? It’s the only way I’ll have the resources to keep up the momentum across the finish line and win in North Carolina – and this is a race we cannot afford to lose._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1566&amount=5&t=9&akid=4122%2E124072%2EW4zYRt)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1566&amount=5&t=10&akid=4122%2E124072%2EW4zYRt)

Thanks so much, Peter. For everything.
Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

clean_body: | | Peter, A year ago, Pete Hegseth dragged every general and admiral to Quantico and embarrassed himself so thoroughly that the Pentagon spent a week cleaning up after it. This week he somehow outdid himself. He rounded up junior officers and enlisted troops to yell about testosterone and "warrior ethos" for an hour - all while completely ignoring the quagmire he's created with Iran, the climbing casualties among our servicemembers, and the widespread destruction of American military bases across the region. From this cartoonish speech, the media quickly latched onto Hegseth rattling off schoolyard insults at American service members about their bodies, their beards, and their identities. | It is heinous, and it is also nothing new from a Secretary who has treated our troops as studio props from the day he was sworn in. Pete Hegseth has one of the most important jobs in the federal government. He is responsible for the stewardship and governance of the world's largest and most powerful military - an agency that employs millions of active duty troops, civil servants, and contractors. Not to mention the millions of veterans served by the VA. But instead of doing that job, he's performing this hyper-partisan, culture war clown show fused with Christian Nationalism. I am sick and tired of this failed Fox News B-string weekend back-up anchor standing up every few months to infantilize and demean military service. Anyone willing to serve this country should be able to. No service member should face ridicule from a man who cannot even figure out how to feed our troops properly. But do not let the insults bury the rest of this dangerous speech. Even though he and Trump just bungled us into a shutdown of the world's oil supply, he stood there bragging about purging 10% of the generals whose counsel might have prevented it. Then promised to double that purge to 20%. He declared "the real battle is spiritual" and built himself a religious affairs office, putting the Pentagon in the business of policing faith in the ranks. He gave our future-of-warfare study to Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich, letting defense contractors write their own shopping list. Each one is a dangerous escalation in his campaign to remake our military in MAGA's image. Hegseth is the most dangerously unqualified man ever to hold this office. He is a likely war criminal who almost certainly would have faced impeachment already if Mike Johnson had not sent the entire House home to smother the articles against him and dodge the Epstein files. And my opponent owns every bit of it. Keith Self enthusiastically endorsed Hegseth's nomination and signed a letter with his MAGA colleagues calling him "an unorthodox yet qualified leader." The fishermen murdered in the Caribbean. The school strike in Minab that killed over 120 children. The sailors left to rot at sea, resorting to attempts to end their own lives. The political persecution and purging of respected commanders. Every single disgrace of the Hegseth Pentagon bears Keith Self's signature - a dishonor doubled by the fact that he should know better as a fellow officer. . [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
When Michigan sent John James to Washington, the expectations were
clear.

He was expected to fight for Michiganders, lower costs, and make life
easier — not harder.

John James is failing all expectations.

Instead of cutting costs, he proudly voted for the tariffs and endless war
in Iran that have cost Michigan households an average of $5,600, and he
voted multiple times to increase healthcare premiums.

He hasn’t just peddled bad economic policy.

John James’ votes in Washington mean people are having trouble finding
ways to afford getting to work. Parents have to stretch to get their kids
to school because fuel prices are over $5 a gallon. Small business owners
are struggling to keep the lights on.

This moment demands a governor who will stand up to the White House’s
dangerous policies and do everything to make Michiganders’ lives better —
not one who’s failed every expectation.

body:
To build power in state legislatures across the country, we need your help to flip these seats in MO, WI, IL, and IA.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261002-1&t=1&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)
Peter,
Republicans are pouring millions into races up and down the ballot, from national to local levels. _Because they know their time in power is coming to an end._
**But in order to secure state power, our candidates in critical Red-to-Blue races need all the support they can get.** With the right resources behind young leaders who refuse to be bought by corporate interests or right wing billionaire donors, and a message that truly connects with working people’s priorities, we can flip these seats.
**That's exactly why our Red-to-Blue Fund exists — to empower bold, young candidates competing in the most critical districts across the country.**
**[Pitch in $5 now to power our Red-to-Blue Fund and fuel the final stretch for our endorsed candidates fighting to flip these seats blue.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&refcode=em20261002-4093&amount=5&t=2&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=3&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
In a must-win election year, these are the races that are essential to break GOP supermajorities and flip state legislatures. Here are a few of the candidates leading that fight:
⭐️ **Cat Clayton** for Missouri, HD-105 ⭐️
⭐️ **Claire Heinrich** for Missouri, HD-110 ⭐️
⭐️ **Leila Staton** for Iowa, HD-54 ⭐️
⭐️ **Nabeela Syed** for Illinois, SD-26 ⭐️
⭐️ **Trevor Jung** for Wisconsin, SD-21 ⭐️
[**](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=4&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)
**Cat Clayton** is a software engineer who has built her career around solving complex issues through collaborative problem solving and careful analysis, and she hopes to bring those skills to MO District 105. She’s tired of watching politicians overturn the will of the people and watching division and misinformation take priority over community good.
The Missouri House is currently in a GOP supermajority. Cat is running to defeat Republican incumbent Colin Wellenkamp and restore balance and accountability to the state house. Cat hopes to bring common sense, compassion, and respect back into government, but she needs your support to help flip this seat.
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=5&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
**Claire Heinrich** was compelled to run for office after watching her representatives ignore constituents and overturn the will of voters. She currently works for a St. Louis nonprofit that teaches middle- and high-school students about active citizenship and problem solving. Claire is driven by her commitment to building stronger communities, and in the Missouri House, she will advocate for investing in public education, infrastructure, and bringing true representation to her constituents.
Claire’s Republican opponent, Niles Stephens, is endorsed by the NRA and MO Right to Live, an anti-choice PAC. And he has aided in ending DEI programs and health education programs in public schools. It is critical that we flip this seat blue. Claire believes that public service should be about listening, showing up, and doing the work, and she needs your help to bring that passion to MO HD-110.
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=6&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
At just 22, **Leila Staton** is the founder of a local advocacy organization that focuses on civic education and engagement. She’s been a dedicated public servant since childhood, and hopes to take that service to the next level by flipping Iowa’s House District 54. Leila is fighting for a government that puts people over profits, community over corporations, and truth over power.
Joshua Meggers is the Republican incumbent in the district. Leila needs your support to flip this seat blue and advocate for public education, clean water, expanding healthcare, and protecting family farms in Iowa’s 54th State House District.
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=7&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
**Nabeela Syed** made history as the youngest member elected to the Illinois legislature, and is a current member of the Illinois State House with the drive to continue her work in the State Senate. In the State House, she has passed legislation to cap prescription drug prices, expand breast cancer screening, increase voter accessibility for young people, and secured paid leave for organ donors. Fun fact, Nabeela was the first state legislative candidate I ever campaigned for! I was in college at the time, and years later when we started Leaders We Deserve, Nabeela was one of the inspirations for the organization.
The seat is currently held by Republican Darby Hills and Nabeela needs support to flip this seat. She’s already proven her commitment to fighting and advocating for her community, and is ready to continue being a hardworking and authentic voice in the State Senate.
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=8&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
**Trevor Jung** currently serves as the City of Racine’s Director of Transit and Mobility, and he’s ready to continue delivering for Wisconsin in the State Senate. He’ll fight to lower costs while raising incomes, provide protections from data center costs, support Veteran programs, and hold Big Tech and Social Media companies accountable.
This seat is currently held by a Republican, and Jim Croft is running to keep it red. So Trevor needs your support to flip this seat and continue making families, neighbors, and communities the priority. This race is especially important to breaking the Republican majority in the State Senate to ensure Wisconsin isn’t the next stop on the GOP’s gerrymandering campaign.
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=9&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
Flipping these red seats blue is absolutely critical to building state legislative power across Missouri, Wisconsin, Iowa, and Illinois. **But these are the kind of bold progressive candidates right-wing billionaires and the corporate machine will come after, Peter.** That’s why I’m asking for your support today — we need grassroots supporters like you showing up to have these leaders’ backs.
**[Will you make a $5 contribution to our Red to Blue Fund today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&refcode=em20261002-4093&amount=5&t=10&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261002_1_r2b.va7F86&amount=5&refcode=em20261002-4093&t=29&akid=4093%2E587540%2ECx2kCl)**
Thank you,
David Hogg
